Everything's fine, chat. That's just the generator kicking on.
It's alright, the trader will come back. They always do.
Oh nice, the deep drill found plasteel. That's huge for us.
Wow, Rook made a masterwork vest. Look at that stat line.
Look at the new dining room. It's so pretty.
Oh yay, the company paid out. That's a lot of silver.
Expedition crew is home. Everybody made it back in one piece.
Hey, welcome in, Static Fern. We're just organizing shelves.
Oh wow, double harvest on the rice. Ivy really came through.
Fertilizer pumps would help this soil a lot. Sadly they're way down the research tree.
Ambrosia bushes popped up by the river. Ivy's going to harvest them gently.
Chemfuel is getting refined at the biofuel refinery. It powers the backup generator during flares.
Little tip for new players. Put a door on every freezer or the cold leaks out.
Cooler room is finally holding temperature. That's three days of tweaking vents.
Everyone's eating at the table now. No more ate without table debuff.
Visiting traders get a little guest room. It keeps them out of the storage area.
Stone cutting is the boring job nobody wants. Pip volunteered, bless him.
Steel is at four hundred and climbing. The deep drill pays for itself fast.
Shelves in the freezer are a game changer. Way more food in way less space.
Hauling is set to priority three for everyone. That way nobody's idle.
Weaponsmithing bench is up and running. Scar's queuing revolvers for the gate crew.
Juno's writing the expedition log. Headquarters wants one after every trip.
Cobalt says hi from the other stream. Hello back, we're planting potatoes.
Muffalo can be milked every few days. Not sure what we'll do with that much milk yet.
Insulated walls aren't a thing in vanilla. So we just build double walls for the freezer.
Every room has a lamp now. Darkness gives people a bad mood.
Herbal medicine is way weaker than industrial. Still better than bandaging with nothing.
Odessa did the expedition paperwork. Four forms, two signatures, one stamp.
Tailor bench is making dusters for summer. Parkas go in storage until the cold comes back.
Pip learned how to cook pemmican. That frees up Mara for fine meals.
Steel walls look cool but they burn. Most people don't know that.
Odd rooms from the gate show up on the map sometimes. We scan them before anyone walks in.
Hospital beds go right next to vitals monitors. They boost healing a little.
Wind turbines need a lot of clear space. That's why they're out past the fields.
Tamsin's building a trade post by the road. Caravans love a short walk.
Gate crew always carries a spare beacon. That way we can find them if things go weird.
Hops sell for decent silver to the outlander towns. So they're basically a cash crop.
Juniper just asked about mood. Bedrooms, food, and beauty are the big three.
Heaters go on the walls of the hospital. Cold patients heal slower.
Expedition loadout is set in the caravan screen. You pick food, gear, and animals there.
Contract board at headquarters refreshed. Three new jobs, all pretty boring.
Scar crafted a bolt action rifle. Good range, slow fire, very his style.
Kitchen now has two stoves. Mara and Pip can cook at the same time.
Floors in the workshop are concrete. Fast to build and easy to clean.
Rook bought a bionic arm from the trader. He's installing it on Bram next week.
Juno, write down everything the gate scanner says. We'll send it to headquarters.
Chat, tell me if the music's too loud. I've been fiddling with the levels.
Mara, bake a few packaged meals for the trip. We leave in two days.
Pip, carry the chemfuel to the generator. Gently, please.
Hollis, rebuild that broken wall with stone. The wood one keeps burning.
Bram, check the deep drill. It might need a new spot.
Ivy, plant the devilstrand in the north field. We'll need it for clothing.
Somebody keep track of the days for me. I always lose count.
Scar, haul the bodies out of the gate room. Somewhere far away.
Tamsin, put a door between the kitchen and dining room. It keeps the dirt out.
Odessa, haggle with the merchant. Use your charm.
Rook, check on Hollis's leg tonight. Make sure it's healing.
Pip wants to try smithing. Should I let him?
Hollis is doing great on cleaning. Do you think he needs a promotion?
We have three spare beds. Should we recruit someone from the next caravan?
Mara wants a bigger kitchen. Is that reasonable right now?
The company is offering a loan. Should we take it?
Gate room power is tight. Should we add another battery?
Odessa wants to go solo to the trader. Is that safe enough?
Juno has the night shift again. Would she rather swap with Bram?
Strawberries or corn in the greenhouse? Has anyone tested both?
Rice has been our whole diet lately. Are people getting bored of it?
Socks keeps stealing food. Can cats even do that?
There's a scroll from headquarters. Want me to read it out loud?
The tailor is idle right now. Should I queue up some hats?
Bram looks bored. Is it time for a hobby room?
We could grow psychoid for trade. Actually no, never mind, is cotton fine instead?
That marble looks gorgeous. Could we afford a marble kitchen?
Our cat seems happy in the freezer. Is that a known cat thing?
Nova suggested a library. Does a library even help research here?
Biscuit is asking about my layouts. Where did I learn this stuff, you ask?
Two caravans arrived today. Which one should we trade with first?
We have a stack of artifacts now. What should we do with them?
Lantern wants to know the best starting crop. What do you all usually plant?
Headquarters changed the form again. Who even designs these?
The workshop's getting crowded. How would you split it up?
Rook's bored between surgeries. What should he craft?
There's an empty room by the gate. What should it become?
Gate scans show three rooms. Which one do we explore first?
Our silver is piling up. How should we spend it?
Mara wants a new recipe. What sounds good to everyone?
The power bill is wild. Why are the sun lamps on during the day?
Okay, wrong stockpile. Let me move that real quick.
Hmm, forgot to put a roof on the barn. Classic me.
Wait, where did the components go. Oh, Rook used them.
I should have built the freezer bigger. Every colony, same mistake.
That's a lot of hats. Too many hats.
Huh, the trader left already. I was still thinking.
Okay, the stove bill was set to zero. No wonder nobody cooked.
Hmm, I can't remember if I paid the contract fee. Let me check.
Note to self, smoothing floors takes forever. Plan ahead next time.
Wait, Pip is a night owl? That explains a lot.
Hmm, that wall looks crooked. I'll pretend I didn't see it.
Okay, let me just double check the caravan list. Medicine, check.
Should have read the form first. Now I signed the wrong line.
Ugh, the turret is facing the wrong way. Fixing that now.
It's okay, we'll replant the corn. One bad harvest isn't the end.
Don't worry about Hollis. His leg is healing nicely.
We're good on parkas. Everyone has one for winter.
Relax, chat, the gate is offline. Nothing's coming through tonight.
No need to rush the research. We're ahead of schedule.
It's alright, that's just a routine memo. Nothing scary from headquarters.
We have enough steel. The drill is still running.
The food situation is fine. Ivy just harvested twenty potatoes.
Hey, don't stress about the timer. The contract has an extension option.
Everybody's mood is solid. Even Pip is happy today.
You're fine, Juno. Take your time with that research.
We've done this run before. The caravan route is safe.
Breathe, chat, the bill just paused. It'll start again soon.
No harm done, the meat's still good. It was only outside for an hour.
Oh, the drill hit another steel vein. We're rich.
Look at Tamsin go. That's the fastest wall ever.
Hey, the contract bonus came through. Extra silver for everyone.
Wow, the greenhouse looks amazing. So much green.
Oh nice, Odessa got the trader down to half price. Great deal.
Finally, the freezer is cold enough. Minus ten, baby.
Juno finished microelectronics at last. That project took forever and a half.
Hey, thanks for the follow, Wren. Welcome to the colony.
Oh wow, a legendary sculpture. Mara is a genius.
Look, the muffalo had a baby. Welcome to the herd.
Wow, Scar finally hit a shot. Proud of him.
Oh hey, look at all that rice. Ivy, you're amazing.
So here's how I set up the work tab for a new colony. Doctoring and firefighting stay at one for anyone who can do them. Then everybody gets one main job, and hauling and cleaning fill the gaps.
Alright, expedition prep checklist time, chat. Food for six days, ten medicine, and parkas even if it looks warm. The gate rooms get cold fast, and nobody wants to walk home freezing.

Headquarters sent the monthly letter, so let me read the important part. They're asking for twenty components and a full report on the gate scans. Honestly that's pretty reasonable compared to last month's request.
Freezer math is simple once you get it. Each colonist eats about one and a half meals a day, so six people need nine. Times a full winter, that's a lot of rice we should be planting right now.
Ivy's the farmer, so she gets the best soil and the first pick of seeds. Pip helps out with the harvest when the fields all ripen at once. Everyone else just stays out of the way of the potatoes.
Trading tip for anyone new to the game. Your social skill changes the prices you get, sometimes by a lot. That's why Odessa does every single deal, even when she's busy with something else.

Research order this run is pretty standard for me. Electricity, batteries, then hydroponics before the first winter hits. After that it's microelectronics so we can finally build the comms console and call traders.

Stockpile priorities confuse a lot of people, so here's the short version. Higher priority zones pull items out of lower ones automatically. That's how food ends up in the freezer instead of rotting on the floor.
Thanks for the follow, Static Fern, really glad you're here. We're doing a quiet building day today, nothing dramatic. Mostly walls, a bigger kitchen, and some very important shelf organization.
Cooking skill matters more than people think it does. A bad cook gives everyone food poisoning way more often. So Mara cooks, Pip assists, and nobody else is allowed anywhere near the stove.
Company paperwork comes in three flavors, honestly. Supply requests, safety audits, and the weird ones that ask about the gate. Juno handles the first two, and I handle the weird ones myself.
Crafting components needs a fabrication bench, which needs a lot of research first. Until then we buy them from traders whenever we can. That's why I always keep about five hundred silver saved up.
Chat, help me keep track of the caravan timeline today. They left on day twelve and should be back around day eighteen. If I forget to check on them, please yell at me nicely.
Mara, here's the plan for the kitchen this week. Simple meals until we've thirty, then switch to fine meals. Also please clean the counters before you start, the room stat is dropping.
Juno, take the research bench in the back room tonight. Finish batteries before you even think about bed. Then leave a note for the morning shift so they know what to start next.
Bram, Scar, grab your rifles and head to the gate room. Just stand guard while the scanner runs its full cycle. Nothing should happen, but I want eyes on that door anyway.
The deep drill is almost done building now. It'll pull steel forever, but it takes a ton of power to run. Should we build another generator first, or just pause the sun lamps for a bit?
Odessa's been doing every trade for weeks now. Her social skill is great, but she's starting to look a little tired. Do you think Juno should learn trading too, just as a backup?
We have a ton of extra leather from all the hunting. Tailoring it into dusters would sell for more than the raw stuff. Is it worth the tailor's time, or should we just sell it as is?
Pip asked for a dog, and honestly I'm thinking about it. Dogs can haul and they're good company for a colony. Would a husky be too much with the muffalo already eating everything?
So the company sent a form with seven pages, chat. Half of it asks about the gate and the rest about our coffee breaks. Which section do you think I should fill out first today?
There's a lot of space left on the east side of the map. I could build a second farm, a barn, or another bedroom wing. What would you all prioritize at this stage of the colony?
Our expedition crew needs a leader for this next trip. Bram is strong, Odessa is social, and Juno is smart and careful. Who would you trust to make the call inside a strange room?
Hmm, I really need to redo this whole storage room someday. The shelves are in weird spots and the doors face the wrong way. Note to self, do it after the gate trip is done.
Wait, I never set the bill for parkas to repeat, did I. That's why the tailor's been idle for two whole days. Fixed now, and nobody saw that, right chat.
Hmm, the cooler room is two degrees warmer than yesterday. Probably the door getting left open by somebody hauling. I'll just add a second door later and pretend it was always the plan.
It's okay, the food looks low but it's really not. Half our meals are in the second freezer, which the counter doesn't show the same way. We're fine for at least two weeks.
Don't worry about the expedition, chat, they're well prepared. Odessa has medicine, Bram has the rifle, and they all have parkas. They'll be home in a few days with loot.

No stress about the company audit this week, honestly. Juno already sorted all the paperwork and filed every report on time. If they ask anything weird, we'll just answer honestly and keep on building.
Hey, it's totally fine if research is slow today. Juno had a really long night and she needs a proper break. We will catch up tomorrow, and the colony isn't going anywhere.
Look at the new dining room, everybody. Long table, flagstone floor, and three sculptures hanging on the walls. This might be the prettiest room we've ever built on this whole stream.
Nice, the trader has components and neutroamine both this time. That is exactly what we've been waiting on all season long. Odessa, go do your trading magic before somebody else buys them.
Gate rooms are basically the core of the company mod. You scan them, prep a crew, and walk through with supplies. Then you bring back artifacts and fill out a very long report for headquarters.
Biscuit asked how I plan bedrooms, so real quick. Four by five, one bed, one end table, and a dresser. Add a lamp and a nice floor, and the mood buffs stack up nicely.
Farming tip for colder maps, if anyone's playing one. Plant fast crops like rice in spring, then potatoes and corn for storage. Hydroponics cover the winter months once you have the power for them.
Electricity is the big early unlock for this colony. Once it's in, we get electric stoves, lights, and real heaters. Everything else in the research tree kind of builds on that one project.
Hauling priorities are where a lot of colonies fall apart. If nobody hauls, stuff sits on the floor and rots. So everyone gets hauling at three, and the busy ones just skip it.
Hollis, start on the new barn walls right after lunch. Wood is fine for this one since the animals don't care. Put the door facing the hay field so the muffalo can graze easily.
Somebody in chat, remind me to check the deep drill in an hour. It sometimes runs out of deposit and just stops. I always forget and lose half a day of steel production.
The stockpile for raw meat is way too close to the dining room right now. Rotting smells give people a bad thought while they eat. Does anyone think moving it to the barn makes sense?
Our silver stack hit two thousand today, which is a record. I could buy weapons, a bionic leg, or a lot of medicine. How would you all spend it if this was your colony?
Huh, the research bench says the tech is already half done. I didn't even notice Juno quietly working on it all night. I'm adding that one to the win column for today.

Little lesson on temperature for anyone who's new to the game. Coolers push heat out one side and cold in the other. If you wall the hot side into the room, you just made a heater. Ask me how I know that one.

Here's what the company actually wants from us this quarter. Thirty steel, ten components, and a written summary of every gate trip. The steel is easy and the components are tight. The summary is going to be me rambling into a form for an hour.

Mara's cooking setup is finally where I want it. Butcher table right next to the freezer door, stove two steps away. The dining room is through one door, so meals barely travel. It sounds small, but it saves her hours every week.

Expedition day is tomorrow, so prep is happening tonight. Bram packs the weapons, Odessa packs the medicine, and Juno checks the scanner logs. Pip loads the muffalo, which takes him forever. It's a whole little routine at this point.

Thanks for the sub, Lantern, that's really kind of you. You're officially getting a bedroom in the brand new east wing. It's four by five with a nice wood floor, a dresser, and a lamp. Honestly it's better than my actual bedroom in real life.

So hydroponics are kind of the backbone of a winter colony. They grow crops indoors as long as the power stays on. Rice grows fastest, and that's what we've got in all twelve basins. Just never let a solar flare hit without a backup.

Stockpile organization is my comfort activity, I'm not even ashamed. Food goes in the freezer, metals near the workshop, and textiles by the tailor. Anything weird from the gate gets its own locked room. Nobody touches that room without telling me first.

Pixel asked how trading works with the company headquarters. You send them goods through the contract board instead of a caravan. They pay in silver, sometimes with a weird bonus item tucked in. It's slower than a trader, but the prices are way more stable.

Ivy's farming plan for the season looks really solid. Rice in the river field, corn on the hill, and cotton out back. Healroot goes in the greenhouse where it's warm. If the weather behaves, we'll have food for a year.

Scar's been crafting all morning over at the smithy. Two maces, a spear, and one very sad looking knife so far. His skill is climbing though, so the quality should get better pretty soon. Everyone has to start somewhere, right, even our worst shooter.

Real quick, let me explain why Hollis never leaves the base. He's our only firefighter with decent speed, and fires spread fast. So he cleans, he builds, and he waits. It's a very quiet job, but he loves it.

Juno's research notes for today are actually really neat to read. She finished batteries and started on the gate resonance project right after. That one unlocks better scanning and much safer expeditions for the crew. Should be done in about three days if nobody interrupts her.

Okay, Pip, here's the plan for your whole afternoon. Haul everything from the crash site into the main storage room first. Then clean the kitchen floor, because it's honestly getting pretty gross in there. After that you can relax and go pet the cat for a while.

Chat, let's do a little vote for the next big project. Type one for a bigger hospital, two for a rec room. Three if you want more shelves, which I already know some of you will. I'll count in about a minute.

Odessa, when the caravan arrives, here's exactly what I want. Sell the extra wool, the tribal hats, and all the spare knives. Buy every bit of medicine and neutroamine they have on them. Don't touch the silver we're saving up for the shield belts.

Juno and Bram both want the bedroom with the window. Juno's been here longer, but Bram works harder. I could flip a coin, but that feels unfair to both of them. Should I just build a second window room instead?

The company sent a contract for forty bundles of cloth. We have the cotton, but the tailor is already slammed with parkas. Taking it would mean pausing winter gear for a few days. Is that a risk you'd take this early in the season?

Hollis wants to learn cooking, which honestly surprised me a lot. He's never shown any interest in the kitchen before today. Mara's willing to teach him on her days off if we shuffle the work tab around. Do you think it's worth trying out for a week or so?

So I have three spots for the new freezer. Next to the kitchen, under the barn, or by the gate room. Each one has a pretty different tradeoff for hauling. Where would you all put it if this was your base?

There's a strange room showing up on the gate scanner today. It reads stable, but it's bigger than anything we've seen. The company wants a full report before we go inside. What do you think we should bring for that trip?

Hmm, I think I set the tailor bill to forever again. That's how we ended up with twenty two parkas last season. Let me just change that to keep ten. Nobody needs twenty two parkas, not even in winter.

Wait, did I ever give the new stockpile any filters at all. That would explain why there are granite chunks sitting in the freezer. Yep, it's set to accept literally everything, classic me. Fixing it right now before Mara walks in and notices.

It's alright, chat, the expedition is just running a little bit late. They had to take the long way around the river because of the flooding. Juno sent a check in from the scanner and everyone's perfectly fine. They should be home by tomorrow evening at the latest.

Don't worry, we've been through plenty of cold snaps before on this colony. Every bedroom has a heater and every single colonist has a parka. The freezer is full, and the hydroponics have a backup power line now. We'll get through this winter just fine together.

Deep drill just hit plasteel and steel in the exact same spot. That almost never happens on a map like this one. Hollis, keep that drill running all night long, please. We're going to be swimming in building materials for the rest of the year.

Look at all those follows coming in, everybody, wow. Welcome to the colony, I'm so glad every one of you is here. We're doing a calm and cozy building stream today. Grab a snack, get comfy, and hang out with us for a while.

Muffalo are honestly the best caravan animals in the whole game, at least for us. They carry a ton of gear and they eat almost anything along the way. They don't panic easily either, which matters a lot near the gate.

Ivy found a patch of wild healroot by the river this morning. Harvesting it now would give us medicine, but transplanting could give us a permanent supply. Should she just grab it, or is replanting it in the greenhouse worth the extra effort?

Alright, let me walk you through how I read a company contract before saying yes. First I check the deadline, because some of them are really tight. Then I check what they want against what's actually sitting in our stockpile. If both look fine, I sign it and hand it to Juno.

Planning the second bedroom wing today, and I have a pretty clear layout in mind. Six rooms in a row, each one four by five with a shared hallway down the middle. Heaters go in every other wall so two rooms share one. It saves a surprising amount of steel and power that way.

Biscuit asked why I always build the hospital near the front door. Injured colonists come back from the gate tired and bleeding, and every step matters. Rook can grab them, patch them up, and get them in bed fast. A short walk can be the difference between a scar and a full recovery.

Cooking for an expedition is different from cooking at home, just so you know. Fine meals spoil within a few days, so they're basically useless on the road. Pemmican and packaged survival meals last much longer and weigh almost nothing. That's why Mara spends a whole day just prepping travel food.

Little peek at the work tab, since a few people asked about it today. Rook is doctor first, crafting second, and basically nothing else after that. Ivy is farming and plants, with hauling at three when she's free. Everybody else just fills in where the colony needs them most.

Tamsin, here's your build list for the next couple of days. Finish the barn roof first, then the new shelves in the storage room. After that, smooth the hallway floor near the dining room. If you finish early, start the walls for the second freezer.

Rook, before the crew heads through the gate, I need you to check everyone. Look for old injuries, infections, anything that might slow them down out there. Pack an extra ten medicine in your bag just in case. Then come find me and give me your thumbs up.

Chat, I want your honest help planning our next caravan trip. Look at the world map with me and pick a town within five days. Tell me if you see anything that looks like a good trade spot. I'll pick the most popular suggestion once everyone has weighed in.

We have about eight hundred silver sitting in the vault right now. A bionic arm for Bram would make him a way better miner and fighter. But we could also buy a full stack of medicine and some components instead. Would you go for the arm, or play it safe with supplies?

Mara has been asking for a proper art studio for a long time. She makes beautiful sculptures, and they sell for really good silver to traders. It would take a whole room and a lot of granite blocks though. Do you think it's worth building it before winter hits us?

So the company is offering us a second gate contract this season. It pays double, but it means sending the crew out twice in one month. Everyone's mood is good right now, and supplies are solid. Is it greedy of me to want to take it?

Juno's thinking about switching research to medicine production next. It would let Rook make industrial medicine at the drug lab instead of buying it. That takes components though, and we're always short on those. Is that a smart move this early in the colony, or should we wait?

Here's a tricky one for all of you watching tonight. Pip is a great hauler but a terrible cook, and he really wants to cook anyway. Letting him practice would make him happier, but the food quality would drop for a while. Should I let him try, just for his mood?

We've got a pile of tribal gear from the early days of the colony. Most of it's worn out and worth almost nothing to traders. I could burn it, or keep it for emergencies if somebody's clothes get ruined. Is it worth holding onto, or am I being a hoarder again?

Odessa just pointed out that our storage room is over capacity again. We could build another room, buy more shelves, or sell off the extra stuff. Each option takes a different chunk of time and silver. Which one would you go with if you were running this colony?

Nova asked earlier how I decide who goes on expeditions. Honestly it's a mix of skills, mood, and who's been home the longest lately. But I'm always curious how other people choose their crews. How do all of you pick who goes out into the strange rooms?

So the trader brought three bionic legs, a shield belt, and a stack of uranium. We only have enough silver for one of those, maybe two if Odessa haggles. Every one of them is useful for the colony in a different way. What would you all grab first, honestly?

Little mystery for chat while I sort the freezer out today. Somebody keeps eating the fine meals instead of the simple ones, and it's draining the stock. I've checked the food restrictions and they all look right to me. Who do you think the secret snacker is in this colony?

Planning out the next season of farming, and I want your opinions. We could go heavy on cotton for clothes, or heavy on corn for long storage. Rice is always in the mix, but space in the river field is tight. How would you split the fields up for the coming year?

There's a new tab in the company headquarters menu I've never seen before. It's labeled internal transfers, and it lists some of our colonists by name. I'm not touching it until I know exactly what it does. Where do you think the company is going with this new feature?

Hmm, hold on, I think I just built the new freezer wall one tile too far over. That leaves a weird little gap right next to the door frame. Nobody's going to notice that except me, probably. Still, I'm fixing it later because it's going to bug me forever.

Wait a second, why is the research bench sitting outside the lab. I could swear I placed it inside the room this morning before the trader came. Yeah, no, I placed it one tile past the wall like a genius. Moving it now and pretending this never happened.

Note to self, stop queuing six different bills at the same workbench. Scar just walks back and forth between them and never actually finishes anything. One bill at a time, in order, with a clear stock limit on each. I keep learning this lesson and then forgetting it.

Hmm, these stockpile zones are getting out of hand, honestly. I have one called food, one called food two, and one called real food. That third one exists because I was annoyed at the first two. I really need to sit down and name these properly someday.

Okay, real talk with myself for a second while the caravan loads up. I forgot the parkas last time and everyone came back with frostbite on their toes. This time they're the first thing on the list, before the food even. Checking it twice, then a third time just to be safe.

Huh, the company letter today is signed by someone new at headquarters. Usually it's the same supply manager every single month without fail. I wonder if they got promoted or moved to another office. Making a mental note to read the next one a little more carefully.

Hey, it's okay that the corn harvest was smaller than we expected this year. The cold came early, and nothing we could have done would have changed that. We still have plenty of rice in the freezer and potatoes in the cellar. Nobody in this colony is going hungry this winter, I promise.

Don't worry about Pip's mood dropping a little tonight, chat. He's just tired from hauling all day, and his bed is still a bedroll. Tamsin is building him a real bed right after dinner. By tomorrow morning he'll be back to his cheerful little self.

It's alright if the trader didn't have what we wanted this time. Another one comes through every couple of weeks, and the comms console can call more. We have enough medicine and components to get by until then. Patience is basically half of this game anyway.

Relax, everybody, the gate scanner just does that flicker sometimes. It's a routine recalibration, and the company manual says it's completely normal. Juno's watching the readings closely, and nothing looks out of place. We'll keep the crew home tonight just to be extra careful.

No need to stress about the company deadline, chat, I've got it handled. Juno and Odessa finished most of the paperwork yesterday afternoon. All that's left is a signature and a count of our steel stockpile. We'll send it off well before the end of the week.

We're doing just fine on power, even with the solar panels down for the night. The batteries are fully charged, and the wood generator is ready as a backup. Hydroponics will stay lit, and the freezer will stay cold. You can all breathe easy, nothing's shutting off.

Hey, I know the expedition took a little longer than usual this time. They found an extra room and decided to scan it carefully before leaving. Everyone checked in on the radio, and they're all healthy and happy. They're walking back now with a whole pile of loot.

It's totally fine that Hollis messed up that wall, by the way. He's still learning construction, and mistakes are how he gets better at it. We have plenty of stone blocks to just rebuild it properly. Nobody's mad, and honestly the wall looks kind of charming.

Don't panic about the empty medicine shelf, I know it looks scary. Rook moved all the medicine into the hospital so it's closer to the beds. There's actually more stock than last week, it's just in a different spot. Everything's under control over here, I promise.

Look at that, the second bedroom wing is completely finished. Six beautiful rooms, every single one with a heater and a lamp. Everybody's mood just jumped up a whole tier at once. This is the cozy colony we've been working toward all season long.

Odessa just sold the jade statue for over a thousand silver. That's the biggest single trade we've ever made on this stream. We can finally afford the shield belts and a bionic arm for Bram. Somebody give that woman a raise right now.

Hydroponics are fully up and running in all twelve basins now. That means fresh rice all winter, no matter how cold it gets outside. Ivy's mood is through the roof, she loves her little indoor farm. What a huge step forward for this whole colony.

Every expedition gets a short name. This one's called the long walk.
Scar woke up on the wrong side of the bed again. Mood penalty, slept on the floor.
Late summer means harvest is close. Everyone's on fields after the run.
Tamsin counted the ceiling tiles in room nine. There are exactly four hundred.
Right now we're in the quiet part of the year. Few raids, decent weather, lots of exploring.
Corridor fourteen splits into five paths. We picked the middle one, obviously.
Pip asked for a pet of his own. Socks isn't interested in sharing.
Quick answer for Pixel, yes, there's a mod settings page. You can tune the gate events there.
Freezing rain is the worst weather in this game. Everything just slows to a crawl.
Defense update, the trap lane is finished. Thirty traps along the east path.
Our gate guard switches every four hours. Nobody stands there alone overnight.
Odessa was the first to see the glowing door. She wrote it down before anyone else.
Expedition rewards came in from the company. Mostly silver and a strange medal.
Ivy's art is getting better each week. The latest sculpture is a hallway with no end.
Raid frequency drops in deep winter. That's my window for long gate runs.
Five more minutes and then break time. Then we're tackling the flooded room.
Tamsin has a cough, though. Is that a real sickness or just flavor?
Turrets are lined up and ready. Does that look like enough coverage to you?

Here's a fun thought. Would you live in the yellow hallway for a million silver?
Odessa's mood is great today. Should she take the deep run?
Heat wave hits tomorrow. Do we push the expedition or wait it out?
Bram found a coin in the corridor. Should we log that as an anomaly?
Chat, real question here. Can you hear the gate hum through my mic?
Juno wants to bring a guitar. Is that allowed on an expedition?
Snow's coming down sideways now. Is that a blizzard or just wind?
Mara found a map in room eight. Could it be a map of the gate itself?
Seasons in this biome are pretty extreme. Has anyone played this mod in the desert?
New raid warning just popped up. Are we ready for this one?

Scar painted the gate room dark green. Does that count as decorating?
Rook came back without his lantern. Where did it go?
Two corridors and one team. Which way do we go?
Company memo says we missed a deadline. When did they even set one?
Mara's been staring at the wall for an hour. What is she thinking about?
Another chat question came in. How do you get the gate in the first place?
Spring storms are rough this year. How many fires is that now?
Turrets keep targeting the wrong spot. Why do they always aim at the trees?
Survey sheet is almost full. Who wants to name the last room on it?
Night shift needs one more person tonight. Who's volunteering?
Hey Bram, go get some sleep. You've been up for a full day.
Everyone, stay on the carpet in this room. The tiles look wrong.
Tamsin, put the anomaly log in the safe. That thing is precious.

Mara, shoot from behind the sandbags. Don't step out.
Odessa, call it in if you see movement. We'll come running.

Pip, bring the extra parka for Rook. He forgot his again.
Scar, let the turrets take the first shots. Then you clean up.
Ivy, don't touch the glowing door. Seriously, leave it alone.
Chat, keep your guesses coming for the room name. I'm writing them down.

Hmm, the coordinates don't match the sketch. One of these is wrong.
Right, so that was a terrible idea. Moving on.
Huh, the gate's quieter than usual. Not sure I like that.
Note to self, build the hospital closer to the gate. Running is slow.
Hang on, Socks is in the corridor again. How does he keep doing that?
Okay, so I misread the forecast. Snow, not rain.
Rook's got this, he knows the hallways. He'll be back in an hour.
Our walls are thick and the turrets are fresh. Nothing's getting through tonight.
Ivy is just napping, not knocked out. She's totally fine.
Missed the last run? That's okay, I'll recap it for you.
Food stores look fine for the season. Nobody's going hungry.
Welcome in, Static Fern. You came at the perfect time.
Gate's humming and the team is ready. Let's go explore.
Look, a room with a sunset painted on the wall. That's actually beautiful.
Raid defeated and the coffee's still warm. Great work, crew.
Alright, back to the map. Where we left off, the team was at the second junction.
Honestly the gate looks better at night. All that blue light against the snow.
Expedition team is resting at the base camp inside. They'll move again at dawn.
Wind is picking up from the west. Turbines are finally pulling their weight.
Tamsin likes to sketch every room we enter. Her notebook is the real anomaly log.
Mood dip across the whole crew today. Too much rain and not enough sun.
Coordinates for room fifty are east thirty, south four. Writing that down twice.
New follower, Ember, thank you so much. You're just in time for the gate.
Kill box rebuild is about halfway. Walls first, then the turret nests.
Defensive towers at each corner of the base. That's the long term goal.
Pip's afraid of thunder, so he's indoors today. Library duty, nice and quiet.
Corridor six is basically a giant parking garage. Empty, echoey, and cold.
So yeah, that's the gate in a nutshell. Power it up, walk in, come back with stories.
Shift changes happen at six and six. Morning crew, evening crew, done.
Bram has been on cleanup for a week. Tomorrow he gets a real day off.
Breaks are every ninety minutes on this stream. That's the rule I made for myself.
Juniper wants to know about contracts. They're like quests, but with company paperwork.
Odd room note, there's a mirror that shows an empty room. No reflection of us at all.
Spring arrived overnight. The snow is just gone.
Ivy's working the research bench all day. She's close to unlocking better turrets.
Today's anomaly is a door that knocks back. Nobody's opening that one.
Hollis built a little bench by the gate. It's his favorite spot to watch the light.
Mortar practice is on the schedule this week. Scar insisted.
Weather's set to clear until tomorrow night. Two good days for surveying.
Mara writes the expedition summary every evening. It's short, but always useful.
Coming up after this, a full tour of the gate room. Then we answer chat questions.
Juno's schedule has a nap at noon. She's more useful after it, trust me.
Raiders brought a siege mortar this time. That changes the plan a bit.

Odessa just leveled up her shooting. Should she take the tower spot now?
Company wants a sample from every room. Do they understand how many rooms there are?
Weather says dry thunderstorm. Should I worry about the fields?

Thirty silver from the trader for one lamp. Is that a good price?

Okay crew, everybody line up at the gate. Headcount before we go.

Everybody, hold up at the junction. Let's make a plan first.

Let me just zoom out a bit. Yeah, that's much worse than I thought.

Odessa just needs a meal and some sleep. She'll bounce back.
Storm or not, the roof is solid. We built it right.
Raiders broke one sandbag. Everything else is totally fine.
Tamsin made it back with all her notes. Nothing lost.
Lights are flickering, but that's just the gate. Normal stuff.
Mood's low, but it's temporary. Good food will fix it.
New corridor unlocked. Let's see where it leads.
Welcome back, Cobalt. We missed you last stream.

Survey number sixty is officially complete. That's a huge milestone.
Mara just caught that thief at the gate. Nice reflexes.

For everyone who just showed up, here's the short version of today. We fixed the turrets this morning and sent a team through the gate after lunch. Then we logged two new rooms before the weather turned on us.
Corridor twelve is one of my favorites, honestly. It's long and narrow with these soft orange lights. And every so often you hear a vent kick on somewhere far away that you can never actually find.
Expedition planning is mostly about food and light. If the team runs out of either one in there, the trip gets really stressful. So I always pack an extra day of meals and two spare lanterns.

So the defense layout works like a funnel, basically. Raiders come in from the road and hit the sandbags first. Then they get pushed into one long lane where four turrets and Scar are waiting for them.
Winter on this map lasts about fifteen days. That's a long time to keep everybody fed and happy. So the rec room gets new games and the kitchen makes fancy meals twice a week.

Mara's schedule is a little unusual right now. She works the fields in the morning and does gate duty in the afternoon. After that she has a long block of free time before bed so she doesn't burn out.

Chat asked earlier how the anomaly log works, so let me explain. Every time something strange happens near the gate or inside it, the game writes an entry. It saves the date, the place, and what we saw.
Coordinates in the gate don't really follow normal rules. You can walk north for twenty tiles and somehow end up south of where you started. Which is why Tamsin writes everything down so carefully.
Break time is coming up in about five minutes. When we get back, the plan is to finish the north wall and check everyone's mood. After that, Rook and Juno go on a short scouting trip.

Today's weather is a mix of everything, apparently. Sunny this morning, foggy at noon. And now there's a thunderstorm rolling in from the hills that's going to make the evening run pretty interesting.
Pip has been doing a lot better lately, mood wise. He's got his own room now with a nice bed. There's even a little shelf where he keeps the odd stuff the team brings back from the gate.
Room thirty seven was genuinely one of the strangest ones yet. It was a full office floor with desks and computers, all switched on. But every screen just showed the same picture of a hallway.
Raids have been coming every five days or so. I've started timing the expeditions around them. So the team is always home and rested when the next group of raiders shows up at the gate.

Okay, here's what I need from everyone on the team. Pack your bags, check your lanterns. And meet me at the gate in ten minutes, because the window closes before nightfall and nobody wants to be stuck in there.
Chat, I could use your help with something real quick. Watch the minimap in the corner while I manage the team. And if any red dots show up near the base, just shout it out for me.
Scar and Odessa, take the two towers on the east side. Rook, stay at the gate with the shotgun. And everyone else, get indoors and stay there until I say the raid is over.
Tamsin, I need the full survey sheet before dinner tonight. Write down every room, every door, and anything weird you noticed, even if it seems small. The company always asks about the small stuff.
Bram, please go check the heaters in every room before the cold snap hits. Some of them were acting up yesterday. And I really don't want anybody waking up with frostbite in the morning.
We've done eight surveys this week, which is a lot. The company keeps asking for more, and the crew is starting to look tired. Should we take a couple of days off from the gate?
There's a door at the end of corridor twenty that we've never opened. Rook keeps walking past it and staring at it, and I keep telling him no. Do you think we should finally try it?
Weather says a heat wave is coming for the next four days. That's usually a bad time for raids, but it's also a bad time for long walks through hot hallways. Is it worth the risk?
Juno has been on every single expedition this season. She says she loves it, and her mood is fine, but I still worry about her a little. Should I give her a break anyway?
Mara and Rook both want to lead the deep run tomorrow. They're equally good at it, honestly, and they both have strong arguments for why it should be them. Which one would you pick?
There are three ways to get past the flooded room, and none of them look great. We can swim, we can climb over the shelves, or we can turn back. What would you do?
Raiders have been hitting the west side a lot more lately. I have enough steel for one more turret or a whole new wall section, but not both. Where would you spend it?
Hmm, that's not right at all. The coordinates say we should be in the lobby. But this is clearly the pool room, and I'm pretty sure the pool room is supposed to be on the other side.
Okay, I need to stop and think for a second. If the gate closes at sunset and it's already afternoon, the team has maybe two hours left. So we turn around soon.
Wait, why is the turret pointed at the barn? I definitely set it to face the road. So either someone moved it or I clicked something I shouldn't have earlier this morning.
Hey, nobody needs to panic about the raid. We've got walls, turrets, medicine, and six colonists who know exactly what to do. So this is going to be a quick one and then we go back to exploring.
Pip's going to be just fine, chat. He had a rough night after the expedition. But he's eating again, he slept well, and his mood is already climbing back up to where it should be.
Don't worry if you missed the earlier part of the stream. The highlights are simple, we found a new room and the team made it back safe. On top of that, the cold snap is finally over.
We actually did it, the whole team made it to the deep corridor and back. Nobody got hurt, and we found three new rooms. Tamsin even filled an entire notebook with notes.
Look at this, the turrets held the whole wave without a single breach. All that work on the walls this week totally paid off. And the crew didn't even need to leave their posts.

Scar's been our main shooter since day one, honestly, and nobody else even comes close. She's calm under pressure and never panics. Even when the big raid came last winter, she just kept firing from the tower. I really trust her up there.
Seasons work a little differently on this map. Spring is short, summer is long and hot, and fall barely lasts a week. Then winter comes in hard and stays for what feels like forever.

Our anomaly log has more than seventy entries now, and it keeps growing. Some of them are small, like a flickering light. Others are bigger, like a door that wasn't there yesterday. I go through them after every run.

Expedition five was the longest one so far, by a lot. The team spent almost a full day inside the gate. They mapped eighteen rooms and found a hallway with real windows. Nobody knows what those windows look out on.
Here's the plan for the rest of the stream. First, we patch up the walls from the last raid. Then we do a short gate run with Mara and Pip. After that, we wind down and do some chat questions.
Rook has a pretty strict routine these days. He wakes up early, eats breakfast alone, and then walks a lap around the base. After that he's ready for whatever job I give him.

For anyone curious, the mod is called Async Industries. It adds the gate, the Backrooms rooms, contracts, and a weird company headquarters. It plays nicely with most of the other mods I'm running too.

So the kill box has three layers now, after this week's rebuild. The outer layer is sandbags and traps. The middle layer is the turret line. The inner layer is just Scar with a sniper rifle, which is somehow the scariest part.

Odessa's mood has been really steady lately, which is really nice to see. She has a nice room, good food, and plenty of free time. She also likes guarding the gate, which surprised me. Some people just enjoy quiet jobs.

Room twenty eight is what we call the waiting room, for obvious reasons. It's full of chairs and magazines from nowhere. There's a little bell on the desk, but nobody ever answers it. We ring it every time we pass.

Chat asked me what happens if a colonist gets lost in the gate. Usually they wander until they find an exit. Sometimes they come out somewhere strange on the map. It's never happened to us yet, thankfully, and I'd like to keep it that way.
Defense work today was mostly small stuff. We fixed two broken turrets, moved some sandbags, and added a door to the kill box. Nothing exciting, but it all matters when the next raid arrives.

Juno is the newest member of the crew, and she's fitting in really well. She joined about twenty days ago after a refugee quest. She's quiet, but she's great with a bow. She's also really good at reading the survey maps.

So the company sends a letter every season, right on schedule. Usually it's a list of things they want from the gate. Sometimes it's a bonus, and sometimes it's a warning. This season's letter was mostly a warning about late reports.

Rain has been falling for most of the week now, without a single break. The fields are soaked and everyone's a little gloomy. Hopefully it clears up before the next expedition. Walking through wet carpet for hours is no fun.

Ivy's been running research every morning, right after breakfast with the crew. Right now she's working on better turrets. After that, she wants to study the samples from the gate. I think she secretly wants to be the company scientist.

Corridor fifteen loops back on itself three times before it lets you out. We only figured that out because Tamsin left chalk marks. The third time we saw the same mark, we turned around. Honestly, chalk saves lives in there.

Break's over, and I'm back at the desk with a fresh glass of water. While I was away, the colony kept running on its own. Mara cooked dinner, Bram cleaned the barracks, and nobody touched the gate. Honestly, that's a really good crew.

Hollis is the person who keeps everything running around here. He fixes the turrets, patches the walls, and repairs the generators. He never complains about it either, not even once. I should really give him a better bedroom soon.

Biscuit asked how often the gate opens, which is a great question. It depends on how much power we give it. With our current setup, it charges once every two days. I'm hoping to speed that up with a second generator.

Raid recap for anyone who missed it. About eight tribals came in from the north road, right around sunset. The turrets took out most of them, and Scar finished the rest. Pip got a small cut, but he's already patched up.

Night shift on this colony is pretty quiet, most of the time anyway. Rook and Ivy usually take it together. They walk the walls, check the gate, and sometimes play chess in the rec room. Honestly, I'm a little jealous of them.

Tamsin's survey notes are really detailed. She writes down the color of the walls, the sound of the lights, and how the air feels. It sounds silly, but those notes helped us find our way back twice already.

Wren just asked if the rooms ever repeat, and the answer is kind of weird. They do, but not exactly. Each copy is a little different, like the chairs moved or a light is off. Tamsin calls them echo rooms, which I think fits.

The muffalo is our oldest colonist, technically, and also the slowest. He's been here since day one. He doesn't do much except eat and wander, but everyone loves him. Pip even built him a little shelter by the river.

Room fifty one is where we found the radio. It was playing a song nobody recognized. We brought the radio back, but it stopped working at the gate. Now it just sits in the rec room, silent, like it's waiting for something.

Mara's been training Juno on expedition stuff for about a week now. They practice reading maps and marking doors. Juno's getting really good at it. I think she'll be ready to lead a run by the end of the season.

Lantern's question was about difficulty settings. I'm playing on a pretty normal setting today, so raids are tough but fair and the gate events aren't too punishing. It's a nice balance for streaming, honestly.

Pip and Juno are good friends now, which happened kind of by accident. They eat together, work the fields together, and even share a bench in the rec room. It's honestly really sweet to watch. Friendships give everyone a little mood boost too.

Our weapons locker is pretty basic right now, and that's something I want to fix. Mostly bows, a few rifles, and one shotgun. Rook carries the shotgun into the gate. Everyone else keeps their bow in case something weird shows up.

Corridor three has a strange smell, according to the log, and everyone describes it differently. Mara called it old coffee and dust. Pip said it smelled like a library. Tamsin just wrote down unknown, which is probably the smartest answer.

Alright crew, listen up for a second, this part is important. Mara and Rook are going in first. Tamsin follows with the survey gear, and Juno stays at the entrance with the radio. Nobody goes past the second junction without checking in.

Chat, if you have questions about the mod, now is a great time. I'm going to be waiting for the gate to charge for a few minutes anyway. Drop them in and I'll read them out. I promise I'll answer every one I can.

Scar, get up in the north tower right now, the raiders are almost at the wall. Odessa, take the south one. Hollis, stand by with the medical kit near the kitchen. Everyone else, inside and away from the windows until the raid is over.

Bram, I need you on the gate controls today, since you know it best. Watch the charge meter and tell me if it drops. If anything weird happens, shut it down right away. Better to lose a day than lose a colonist.

Juno, take the long route back through corridor six, the one with the orange lights. The short route is flooded right now. Keep the lantern up and follow the chalk marks. You'll be home before it gets dark, I promise.

Everyone, please take a meal break before the run, and I really mean everyone. You've all been working since sunrise. Sit at a table, eat something warm, and rest for an hour. We'll head out once the sun is a little lower.

Tamsin, please copy the survey sheet before we send it to the company. They lost the last one somehow, and they never told us why. I want our own record of every room. That map took us two whole weeks to make.

Rook, slow down in this next hallway. The floor tiles look different here, kind of shiny and too clean. Step only on the carpet and keep your hand on the wall. If anything shifts, just stop and call out to the others.

Ivy, before you start research today, check on the samples in the freezer. One of them was glowing last night. If it's still glowing, move it to the shed by itself. Then write it up in the anomaly log.

New folks, here's how you can help the colony, even from the chat. Watch for raid warnings in the top corner. Suggest names for every new room we find. And if you see something weird, tell me, because I miss a lot.
Pip, go sit with Odessa for a while, just keep her company. She had a long shift at the gate and her mood is dipping. Bring her a warm meal and maybe a book. Company helps more than you'd think.

So the company offered a new contract today, and it's a big one. It pays really well, but it means a three day expedition. That's longer than we've ever stayed inside the gate. Do you think the crew is ready for that?

Juno found a second key inside room forty, tucked under a desk. It's the same shape as the first one, just a different color. Tamsin thinks they open the locked door in corridor twenty. Should we try them both tonight?

There's a big raid warning for next week, and it looks like a big one. I could spend the time building more defenses. Or I could send one more expedition before it hits. Is it smart to risk the team right before a raid?

Odessa wants to move into the room by the gate, of all places. She says the hum helps her sleep. It's a little strange, but her mood has been great lately, so maybe she's onto something. Should I just let her do it?
Chat voted for the green door last time we had a choice like this. It led to a room full of plants, which was lovely. Now there's a blue door and a red door ahead of us. Do we let chat pick again?

The forecast says the cold snap ends tomorrow, finally. That would give us a nice window for a long survey. But the forecast was wrong last week too, by almost two whole days. Can we really trust it this time?

Mara's been talking about building a small camp inside the gate. A place to rest halfway through long runs, with beds and a stove. It would take a lot of materials and time. Is that worth doing this season?

Bram got into a fight with Hollis this morning, right in the middle of breakfast. It was small, just about who gets the warm bed. They're both fine now. Should I build a second warm room so it doesn't happen again?
We've got enough silver for one big purchase, and only one. We could buy a new turret, a set of armor, or a bionic arm for Hollis. Each one would really help in its own way. Which one would you pick?
The company sent a memo that just says report to headquarters. No details, no reason, no deadline, and I've read it five times now. What do you think they actually want from us?

Every time we go deeper into the gate, the rooms get stranger. The last one had grass growing out of the carpet. The one before that had a ceiling made of clouds. What do you think is at the very bottom?

Chat has been asking about my defense layout all stream, which I love. Some of you want more turrets, some want more walls. A few of you want a moat, which is honestly tempting. How would you design it?
Juno and Pip are both asking for the same job this season, and I can't split it. They both want to be the expedition cook. Juno's a better cook, but Pip loves it more. Who should get the job?
There's a strange hum coming from under the kitchen. It started after the last gate run, and nobody else has heard it except Mara. Where do you think it's coming from?

Let me just check the numbers again, because I don't trust myself right now. Six colonists, four turrets, two towers, and one cat. That should be enough for a small raid. Unless they bring the big guys, which they always do.
Hmm, wait a second here. That door wasn't on the survey map yesterday, and Tamsin's notes are always right, so the door must be new. That's either really cool or really bad.
Note to self, never schedule an expedition during a heat wave again. The team came back exhausted and cranky, Pip got heatstroke, and Rook drank all the water. Lesson learned, the slow way.
Yeah, so I kind of messed that up, and I'm not even surprised. I put the turret on the wrong side of the wall. Now it can only shoot at our own garden. I'll move it once this raid is over.

Let me think about this for a second, out loud so chat can follow. If the team leaves at noon and the gate closes at dusk, that gives them six hours. That's enough for maybe five rooms. Maybe four if Rook gets distracted again.
Huh, the anomaly log just added an entry by itself. I didn't see anything happen, and it just says something moved near the barn. Great, that's not creepy at all.

Take a breath with me, everyone, because this looks worse than it's. Hollis is hurt, but he's in a medical bed already. Ivy's treating him with good medicine. He's going to be up and walking again in a couple of days.

Chat, it's really okay that we lost the expedition samples. They were nice to have, but the crew is safe. That's what actually matters to me, every time, like a ritual. We'll get more samples on the next run anyway, I'm sure of it.

Don't worry about the power going out like that, chat. The generators just need fuel, and Bram is already hauling wood. The gate will keep its charge for a while. We have plenty of time to get it back up.
Hey, the raid looks scary on the map, but we've got this. The turrets are fully repaired, and Scar is in the tower. Everyone else is inside where it's safe. This will be over in a minute, I promise.
Rook's mood is low right now, but it's not a big deal. He just missed a meal and slept on the floor. A hot dinner and a real bed will fix it. He'll be back to normal by morning.

If you're worried about Juno, she's totally fine. She came back from the gate a little shaky, but she's resting now. Mara's sitting with her in the rec room. Give her a night, and she'll be ready to go again.

Look, the blizzard sounds bad, but we planned for it. There's food in the freezer, wood in the stockpile, and heaters in every room. Everyone's inside and warm, even Socks. We just wait it out together, nice and cozy.

This is a huge moment for the whole colony. The research just finished after three long days, and we finally unlocked the upgraded turrets. They shoot faster and they don't explode when they break. Our defenses just got so much better overnight.

Welcome to all the new folks coming in from the raid. There's a lot happening right now, so let me catch you up quick. We're about to send the whole crew through the gate together. You picked the perfect time to show up.

Wait, look at the anomaly log right now. It just added three brand new entries at once, all in a row. Every single one of them is from the same room. That room is officially the weirdest place we've ever found.

The crew is finally home after the long expedition. Three whole days in the gate and every single person made it back. Tamsin's notes are amazing, and Rook found a working radio in a closet. This is the best run we've ever had.

Spring is here and the snow is finally gone. The fields are ready, the river is flowing again, and the traders are already coming back. Everyone's mood just jumped up across the whole base. This is going to be a great season.

The company actually liked our survey report. They sent a bonus, a brand new contract, and a little medal just for Tamsin. She's going to be impossible to live with now, and I don't even care. I'm so proud of this crew.

Mara just finished the last stone bed in the barracks, and every colonist finally has a real place to sleep. Six months ago they were sleeping on dirt. Chat, we really built something here.

Last night I coded until the birds started singing outside, which wasn't the plan. My cat sat on my lap the whole time like a tiny supervisor. I regret nothing.
Biscuit, you said you feel behind everyone else your age, and I get that. Comparing yourself to other people's highlight reels is exhausting. You're right on time for your own life.
Everybody, drop a little heart in chat for Static Fern, they had a brutal week at work. Let's flood it a bit. Kindness is free and we've got plenty of it.
Wren has been here since the very first stream, back when I had three viewers and one of them was my cat on another tab. Seeing that name pop up still makes my day. Thank you for staying.

Note to self, never promise chat an early night, because it never happens. It's two in the morning again. Socks is judging me from the bed. She's been asleep for an hour and still somehow looks disappointed in my choices.

Juno, I know the breach was terrifying, and you were so brave to pull Ivy out. It's okay that your hands are shaking now. That's just the fear leaving. Sit down by the fire with Mara and let it pass, we'll handle the rest tonight.

We got through the whole winter without losing a single colonist, and that's huge for this map. Last year I lost two people to the cold. This time we planned, we stocked up, and you all helped me remember the heaters.
We've got a new kitten in the colony, and she's tiny and gray and perfect. Socks watched her through my screen and approved. Should we let chat vote on her name tonight?

Hold on, Odessa just walked into the dark room all by herself. No panic, no shaking, she just went in and grabbed the medicine. A month ago she couldn't even look at that door without crying, so this is massive. I'm so proud of her.
Coding today was mostly me staring at one error for three hours. Then I realized I'd spelled a word wrong. That's the whole story, and I'm still a little embarrassed.
Hey, Lantern, losing a pet is one of the hardest things there is. You loved her and she knew it. Stay here with us as long as you need tonight.
Honestly, the music I've been listening to lately is all soft synth and rainy piano. It makes late night building feel like a movie. If you've got recommendations, I'm always listening.

Hollis, take Pip outside and show her the sunflowers. The bugs are gone and the yard is completely safe now, I checked twice. She hasn't seen daylight since the expedition. Go slow, and let her hold your hand if she wants.
Every time someone in chat says this stream helped them through a bad night, I sit with that for a while. It means more than any follow or sub ever could. You all made this place, not me.
Rook wants to build a tiny shrine for the colonists we lost, up on the hill. I think it would help everyone heal. Does that sound good to you all?
Cobalt said he hasn't doomscrolled for a whole week, and he spends that time here instead. That might be the nicest compliment this stream has ever gotten. Welcome to the healthier habit, buddy.
Tamsin wandered into the kitchen at midnight and made tea for everyone on night watch. Nobody asked her to, she just noticed they were cold. That's the kind of colonist you build a whole base around.
Moss, being laid off doesn't mean you weren't good at the job. Companies make choices that have nothing to do with you. We'll be right here cheering when the next thing comes along.
Chat, the colony finally has a proper music room with a piano and two drums. Ivy keeps sneaking in there to practice when she thinks nobody's watching. Would you all help me name the room after her?

Okay, real quick, the kettle just clicked so I'm grabbing tea. My cat already stole my chair the second I stood up. This is her stream now. Keep an eye on the colony while I'm gone, and yell if a raid shows up.
Scar has been carrying the trauma from that first gate for weeks, and today she laughed at one of Bram's terrible jokes. Small thing, but it felt like sunrise. Healing is slow and that's okay.

Wait, Wren just gifted five subs to random people in chat. Somebody who had a rough day might've just gotten one, and honestly that's the most beautiful thing ever. That's so generous, thank you. Everybody say a huge thanks to Wren.

Real talk for a second, some of you have been showing up every night during really hard stuff. Breakups, lost jobs, sick family. You keep coming back, and I'm honored that this is where you feel safe.
Pip's been asking for a room of her own with a little window and a reading lamp. She's been so brave lately, so I want it to be special. What should we call it?
Socks has a new favorite spot right on top of my router, which explains the lag tonight. She's warm, she's happy, and I don't have the heart to move her. Sorry, chat, the cat outranks the internet.

Hollis, Mara, Rook, everybody gather around the fire tonight. The company sent bad news, but we'll read it together. Grab a warm meal and a blanket first, because it's long and kind of grim. Nobody faces that letter alone.
There's a quiet patch of meadow by the river that I keep looking at. It would be perfect for a little picnic spot with benches. Do you all think that's worth building tonight?

Little personal update, I finally finished the music player I've been coding for months. It's ugly and it only plays one folder, but it's mine. Tonight's whole playlist is running through it, so if it crashes, you'll know why.

Odessa sat with Ivy for three hours after the breach and didn't say a single word. She just held her hand and hummed. Sometimes that's all comfort needs to be, and watching it made me tear up a little.
Nova, I'm really sorry the move fell through, that's such a heavy thing to carry. You've rebuilt plans before and you'll do it again. For tonight, though, just hang out and help me pick floor tiles.

Rook and Pip have this little ritual where they check the turrets together every evening. He lets her carry the flashlight, and she tells him which wall looks the bravest. I've never seen anything sweeter on this map, and I've watched a muffalo adopt a duckling. Pip giggles each time, no exceptions.

Okay, the new mess hall is finally done with long tables and a fireplace at the end. Everyone can eat together for the first time in this colony's history. It feels like it deserves a proper name from chat. Can you all help me pick one?

Some of you mentioned you're up late because you can't sleep, and I totally get it. My brain does the same thing most nights, which is half the reason I stream this late. So we're insomnia buddies now. That's official.

Bram, the fire's out and everyone got out safe, including the dog. The kitchen can be rebuilt, the stove can be replaced. You can't be replaced, so please stop blaming yourself. Come sit down and let Mara look at your hands.

Coming back to this colony every night feels like visiting old friends. Tamsin still waves at the camera when I zoom in, and I'm pretty sure that's not a real game mechanic. I'm choosing to believe she knows we're watching. It makes the whole place feel alive.

Chat, real quick, if you've got a friend who's struggling tonight, send them a message after the stream. It doesn't have to be fancy, a simple hey, thinking of you works. People remember those little texts for years. Trust me on that one.

Late nights like this remind me why I started streaming in the first place. Back then I was coding alone in a dark room with my cat and no one to talk to. Now there's a whole chat full of kind people keeping me company. That still kind of blows my mind.

Biscuit just posted that she passed her driving test on the third try. Three tries, and she never gave up once. That's exactly the kind of energy this colony runs on. Everybody give Biscuit some love in chat right now.

Ivy's been terrified of the gate since she came back from the first expedition. Today she stood next to it and helped Rook carry supplies through. Her mood bar dipped for a minute, then climbed right back up. That's what courage looks like in this game.

Hmm, my cat's staring at the wall behind me like there's something there. That's either a bug in my apartment or a ghost from the Backrooms. Either way, I'm not turning around. We're going to keep building and pretend I didn't notice.

Cobalt, I'm so glad your grandpa's surgery went well, you were worried all week. Seeing you come back to chat with good news made my night. Give him a hug from everyone here. We were rooting for him the whole time.

There's a trader at the gate offering a little white puppy for almost nothing. Our colony could absolutely use a guard dog, even a tiny fluffy one. Pip already ran out to pet her before I clicked anything. Should we just adopt her right now?

Tamsin, I know the trader said your old home was gone, and that hurts so much. You're allowed to grieve it as long as you need. This place isn't a replacement, but it's a home too. Everybody here loves you and they'll show you that.

Funny thing about coding at three in the morning is that every idea feels brilliant. Then I look at it the next day and wonder who wrote it. Usually it's half genius and half nonsense. My cat's notes on the keyboard don't help either.

We're building a garden for the colonists we've lost, with flowers for each of them. I want it to feel peaceful, not sad, just somewhere quiet to remember. Chat, you knew them almost as well as I did. What flowers do you think each one would have liked?

The company just approved our first big contract and sent a bonus crate of supplies. There's medicine, warm clothes, and a whole box of chocolate in here. Mara's already hiding the chocolate from everyone else. Today's officially a good day.

Music has carried me through so many rough nights, and that's why it's always on during streams. Some of these songs got me through finals, breakups, and a really lonely winter. Sharing them with you all now makes them feel happier. It's like they found new homes.

So I've been thinking about doing a little community night where chat helps design a whole room from scratch. You'd pick the furniture, the colors, even who gets to sleep there. It'd be slow and cozy with no raids allowed. Would anybody actually show up for that?

Static Fern, a panic attack at work doesn't make you weak, it means you've been carrying too much. You took care of yourself by stepping away, and that's the right call. We're glad you're here now. Just breathe and watch the muffalo wander around.

Everyone who's new tonight, go introduce yourself in chat if you feel like it. No pressure at all, lurking is perfectly fine too. This community is really gentle and welcoming with newcomers. You'll find your people here fast, I promise.

Okay, I need to remember to back up my code files tonight, because last month I almost lost everything. My cat walked over the delete key and I nearly cried. Note to self, cats and keyboards should not mix. She's watching me type this right now.

Moss said this is the first stream he's watched since his dad passed, and he just wanted somewhere calm. That means so much that you'd come here. We'll keep it slow and peaceful tonight. Take all the time you need with us.

Hollis wants to paint a mural on the dining room wall, but he can't decide what to paint. I've told him chat will help, because you always come through. He's already mixing colors in the corner. Should it be the colony, the gate, or all of us around the fire?

Scar's been teaching the new kid to garden every morning before chores. They kneel in the dirt together while Scar explains each plant like it's a person. The kid follows her everywhere now. Isn't that the sweetest thing you've ever seen in this game?

Real question for the regulars who've been here since the beginning. Remember the colony where everyone lived in one giant bedroom? This base is so much cozier, but I miss that chaos sometimes. Do you think we should build one big sleepover room for old times' sake?

Before you head out tonight, chat, do one kind thing for yourselves. Maybe it's a glass of water, a shower, or just going to bed on time for once. You've been so kind to everyone here all stream. Save a little of that kindness for you too.

After a whole week of setbacks, the new bedroom wing is finished. Every colonist gets their own room now, with a bed, a dresser and a little lamp. Pip already decorated hers with seashells. I'm so happy I could just sit here and watch them sleep.

Chat, the quest is complete, the company finally paid us, and the freezer is completely full. That basically never happens all at once around here. So I think we should just enjoy it for a minute. How often does everything go right at the same time?
