So I just checked the expedition log, and the last entry from Juno says the hallway keeps going. After that there's nothing, just static. I think we have to accept she's not walking back through that gate.
Mara was the first colonist I ever drafted in this run. She fought off the very first raid with a wooden club and a lot of attitude. Burying her today feels like closing the first chapter of a book.

We're wrapping up the colony tonight after almost three hundred days. I spent the afternoon walking every pawn through their favorite rooms one more time. It's silly, but it felt like the right way to say goodbye.
Biscuit followed Pip everywhere for years, even into the gate room. When Pip passed, Biscuit just stopped eating and slept on his bed. Last night he went too, and honestly that one really got me.

Pixel told me this will be their last stream because life is getting busy. They've been here through four colonies and so many terrible raids. I'm happy for them, but I'm definitely going to feel that empty spot in chat.
Okay, I'm just gonna sit here on the funeral screen for a minute. I know it's a game and I know they're pixels. Still, Hollis felt like a real part of this little family.
We lost Scar during the breach and the base feels so different now. Even the turrets look kind of lonely without him patrolling. Do you think the others can feel it too, or is it just me?

Rook's expedition was supposed to be a quick supply run through the blue rooms. It's been six days and the tether finally snapped this morning. Is there any chance at all that he's still wandering around in there?
Tamsin and Bram were married for most of this colony, and now they're both gone. I put their graves side by side under the big oak tree. What would you all want carved on the stone for them?
Hey, Lantern, I saw your message about missing your old dog tonight. You don't have to be cheerful on my account, okay? We can just hang out quietly and build some furniture together for a while.
I know a lot of you loved Ivy, so this one hurts for everybody. She lived a good long life and she got to see the garden bloom. We'll plant something new there in her honor tomorrow.

Okay, so this is it, chat, the very last day of the Thornfield colony. We started with three broken people in a crashed pod and a bag of rice. Now look at it, all stone walls and gardens and graves of people we loved. I'm really going to miss this place.

Scar's death message just popped up and I genuinely had to stop for a second. He was the one who dragged everyone out of the first gate collapse. He never complained, never broke, just kept carrying people. I don't know who's going to fill those boots.

Socks the cat has been with us since day four, and she passed in her sleep tonight. She was old and comfy and probably very full of stolen fish. Honestly that's the best way out anyone could ask for. Still, the base feels a lot quieter without her.

Moss has been modding this chat for three whole years, and today's their last day. They're starting a new job and won't have evenings free anymore. Every inside joke in this chat has Moss somewhere in its history. Thank you so much, friend, for everything you did here.

We dug the fourth grave this week and I just ran out of good words. Mara, Pip, Bram, and now Odessa, all from one awful winter. I keep thinking about what I could've done differently with the heaters. Let's just give them a quiet minute before we keep playing.

Expedition team two was gone for twenty days, and only the radio came back through the gate. It just plays the same three notes over and over now. I'm keeping it on the shelf in the gate room anyway. It feels like the closest thing to having them home.

Hollis turned eighty today in game, and I knew this day was coming. He was our first doctor and he patched up every single one of us. He went peacefully with Ivy holding his hand in the hospital. I'm not crying, the room is just really dusty.

Note to self, never let a colony get this attached to a single muffalo. Big Bertha carried our caravans across four seasons without one complaint. And now she's gone and I'm looking at an empty barn. Okay, yeah, I'm a little sad about a cow buffalo.

Juno just stepped through the gate to bring back the medicine for the others. The gate shut behind her and the signal went flat. Everybody survived because of what she did in there. Do you think we should name the next colony after her?

We're shutting the colony down after almost a year of streams. I'm proud of it, but closing the save file feels like leaving a home. I made a little highlight reel of all our best moments. Would you want to watch it together before we start something new?

Pip was the kid who grew up on this stream, chat. We watched him go from crawling around the kitchen to running the whole research lab. Tonight the raiders got him, and I'm still kind of numb. How do you even say goodbye to somebody you watched grow up?

Nova just told me this is their goodbye, they're moving and won't have internet for a while. They've been here since I had like four viewers total. I genuinely don't know what streams will feel like without them saying hi. Where do I even start with thanking someone like that?

I know it feels awful watching Rook's portrait go grey after all that. He made it two hundred days in a world that tried to eat him. That's a good story, and we got to watch every bit of it. He'll stay in our memories as long as this chat does.

Two hundred and eighty days, chat, and tonight we finally retire this colony. We survived raids, plagues, three gate breaches, and one very angry turkey. I'm so proud of every single colonist who lived here. Thank you for being part of this whole wild journey.

Ivy's eating dinner at the table with a fork, like a civilized person. Rook, meanwhile, is eating raw rice off the floor next to the muffalo, and he looks proud of himself. Same colony, chat, same exact colony, same dinner bell.

Okay, quick catch up for anyone who just walked in. We're on day thirty in the colony, there are six of us. And the company keeps mailing me contracts I didn't ask for. Right now I'm just trying to get the freezer finished before the heat wave hits.

So last stream ended kind of abruptly, and I owe you the story. Mara went through the east gate alone because I misclicked her into the expedition. She came back two days later with a lamp, a lighter, and absolutely no explanation. We still don't know where the lamp came from.

Here's the plan for tomorrow in game. Rook hauls stone all morning, Pip builds the second wall on the storage room. And I handle the research bench. If a trader shows up, we buy steel and nothing else, no matter how cute the hats are.

Somebody in chat asked why I keep the gate room locked at night. Honestly, it's because things come out of it after dark that I don't want wandering into the kitchen. What would you put in front of it, a turret or a really stubborn door?

Welcome in, Lantern, you picked a calm moment. We just finished harvesting the rice and everybody is eating at the same time for once. Nothing is on fire, nobody is crying, and the company hasn't sent paperwork in almost a full day.

Alright, Bram, I need you off the sculpture and onto the generator right now. The fuel is getting low and the night shift is going to be dark without it. Go fix it, then you can go back to making your weird little statue of a muffalo.

For people catching up, the big building on the left is the company office. We didn't build it, it just appeared after the second contract. Inside there's a desk, a chair, and a phone that rings at exactly noon every single day.

Note to self, the cooler goes on the outside wall, not the inside one. I did it backwards last time and cooked the whole pantry. Moving it now before anybody notices, because I have a reputation to protect.

Tomorrow is mostly a building day. I want the hospital finished, three beds, a vitals monitor if we can afford it, and a proper door this time. Last time the door was a curtain, and Hollis walked through it carrying a bear.

Juniper is asking if we're doing another expedition tonight. Probably, but only after the crops are in and Ivy is healed up. Does that sound fair, or do you want me to just send everyone through the gate and hope for the best?

So here's what happened while the stream was off. Nothing, actually, because I don't play off stream. I know some of you thought I was secretly grinding, but the colony freezes the moment I stop talking to you.

Alright, the trader's here, and let's see what they've got. Medicine, some cloth, a bunch of wood we don't need, and one very expensive painting. We're getting the medicine, because last week taught me that lesson twice.

Chat, keep an eye on the top corner of the map for me. Something has been moving around near the old mine and I can't tell if it's an animal or something worse. If you see it come closer, say so loud.

For anyone new, the rooms past the yellow door are the odd ones. Some of them repeat, some of them get bigger when nobody's looking. And one of them hums. We mostly use the humming one for storage now, because it keeps bread fresh.

Okay so the quest letter says we can escort a stranger to the north edge for a pile of silver. It also says the stranger is wanted by three different factions. Which part of that do you think I should be worried about first?

Real quick, let me explain the shift schedule because people keep asking. Day crew is Scar, Pip, and Tamsin, and night crew is Rook and Odessa. Juno sleeps whenever she wants, because she's the doctor and nobody argues with her.

Last stream we lost the power for most of the night. And I never told you why. It turns out Socks the cat was sleeping on the battery bank. Every time she rolled over, something flickered, and I spent an hour blaming the wiring.

Hmm, the stockpile is filling up faster than I thought. I might need a second shelf room. Or I could stop letting Pip haul every rock he sees, which is honestly the cheaper option and also the funnier one.
So the plan for the next in game day is simple on paper. We dig the new tunnel toward the yellow rooms, set up lights every few tiles, and leave a door at the end. Then we wait and see what knocks.

Moss asked what the company actually wants from us. As far as I can tell, they want reports, samples from the odd rooms, and for us to sign things nobody has time to read. They pay well, though, so I'm signing things.

Okay, everybody inside before the cold snap starts. Tamsin, close the barn, Hollis, light the heaters, and someone please drag Rook out of the field because he's trying to finish one more row. Nobody's freezing tonight.

Here's the short version of the colony so far. We crash landed, built a shack, found a gate, signed a contract with a company that has no face, and now we have a cat. That's pretty much the whole story.

I'm going to queue the research while it's quiet. Electricity first, then refrigeration, then whatever the company paperwork keeps calling anomaly containment. It sounds important, and it also sounds like something I'll regret skipping.
Wren wants to know if we can rename the cat. We could, technically, but Socks has been Socks since day one and she absolutely knows her name by now. Would you really do that to her?

Alright, morning in the colony, and everybody's waking up slow. Odessa is already at the stove, Bram is staring at the wall, and Pip is somehow outside in his pajamas again. Standard Tuesday, I think, at least by our standards.
So last time, if you missed it, we found a room in the odd wing that only had a chair. Just a chair, in the middle of a huge empty floor. Nobody sat in it. And I still think that was the right call.
Okay, I keep forgetting the zone for the hay. It's getting stored next to the meals again, which is a whole problem. Fixing that now, quietly, so nobody in chat sees it and starts typing at me.

Tomorrow I want to try a short expedition with just two people. Scar for the shooting, Juno for the patching up, and nothing heavy in their bags so they can run. If it goes well, we send a bigger team the day after.

Okay, chat, tactical question for you while things are calm. We have enough steel for either a turret by the gate or a proper freezer for the meat, and not both. Which one do you think keeps us alive longer?

Hey Cobalt, welcome back, you missed a quiet hour. We moved the beds, fixed the roof over the kitchen, and argued with the company phone for a while. Now we're waiting on a caravan that might or might not show up.

Let me walk you through the defense setup, since a few people asked. Sandbags at the front, two turrets near the gate room, and a long hallway that makes raiders walk single file. It isn't pretty, but it works most days.
Ivy, put the gun down and go eat something. You've been on guard for twelve hours and the food meter is in the red. The wall will still be there when you get back, I promise.

So the company sent a form today asking us to rate our satisfaction. There were five little boxes, and none of them said confused. I picked the middle one, because that felt the most honest thing I could do.

Plan for the night is to keep things boring. Lights stay on in the odd wing, nobody opens the yellow door, and Rook guards the gate with a thermos. If it stays boring, I'll be very proud of all of us.
Wait, I put the bed in the freezer. Why is there a bed in the freezer? Okay, it's moved now, and we're all pretending that didn't happen, especially the person who built it.

For anyone catching up, Hollis is the tall one with the beard and the very calm face. He's our hunter, our cook on weekends. And the only one the muffalo actually trusts. He also hasn't said a single complaint all colony, which is suspicious.

Answering Pixel's question about difficulty, we're playing on the middle setting with the company mod turned up a bit. Raids hit hard but never feel unfair. The odd rooms are where most of the real danger comes from, honestly.

Alright, the expedition team is home and their bags are full of strange stuff. Two metal cubes, a flashlight that's always warm, and a map of a room we haven't found yet. Where do you think that map leads?

So the routine for the next day goes like this. Wake up, eat, Juno checks everybody's injuries, and then we split into builders and haulers. In the afternoon, Scar and I go look at the new door that showed up near the well.

Quick recap for Static Fern, who just got here. We survived a raid this morning, one person got hurt but she's fine, and we found a hallway that loops back on itself. That's the whole afternoon so far.
Somebody remind me to check the food at the top of every hour. Last time I forgot for a whole in game week and we ended up eating berries and sadness. Chat, you're officially my alarm clock now.

Story time from last stream, since someone asked about the fridge. Pip tried to build a fridge out of the cold room in the odd wing. It worked perfectly for two days and then the room moved about ten tiles to the left.

Biscuit is asking whether the gate ever closes on its own. It does, but apparently only when nobody's watching it, which is a very rude habit for a door. Have any of you actually seen it close, or is that just me?
Alright, building the new barracks now. Six beds, two dressers, one lamp per corner, and a rug because Odessa asked very politely. It's going to be the nicest room in the colony by a lot.

Okay so the plan for the next contract is pretty straightforward. We walk in, grab the sample from the third room, and walk out. Nobody touches the vending machine, because last time it ate a colonist's sleeve.
Hmm, that wall should be stone, not wood. Wood right next to the generator is just a fire waiting for an excuse. Swapping it before I forget again, because I'll forget again.
For the newcomers, the little pen by the river is for the muffalo. Her name is Pudding, she's very old, and she gets the warmest spot in the barn. That's not really strategy, I just love her.
So a few of you asked about our power setup, and here it's. Two solar panels, one wind turbine, and a pile of batteries in a shed that's half underground. What would you add first if you were me?

Last stream ended right as the solar flare hit, so here's what happened after. Everything went dark for a day, the freezer warmed up, and we ate a lot of fast meat. Nobody got sick, which honestly feels like a small miracle.
Rook, Pip, both of you head to the south field with the axes. We need firewood before the cold settles in tonight. Come back before dark, and bring whatever berries you find on the way.

Alright, so to explain the expedition rules for anyone new here. Two people minimum, one medic kit each, and nobody goes past the third door without checking with me. I made those rules after we lost track of Bram for a week.
Hey Nova, welcome in, grab a seat. We're in a slow stretch right now, just sorting the stockpile and fixing a few broken chairs. It's good timing if you like calm streams and very small decisions.

Tomorrow's job is the kitchen expansion. Two stoves instead of one, a butcher table that isn't next to the beds, and a door that actually closes. Odessa has been asking for this for weeks, and she deserves it.
Okay, the raid timer says soon. Turrets loaded, doors closed, people fed, cat hidden in the bedroom. Alright, I think we're actually ready this time, which feels strange to say out loud.
Since people keep asking, the colony's main goal right now is to map the odd wing. We've found nine rooms so far and the company wants twenty. I'm not sure there even are twenty, but we'll see.
So the trader asked for two hundred silver for a single bionic arm. I don't have two hundred silver, I've about forty and a nice rug. We said no and they left looking very disappointed in us.
Moss suggested we build a second gate room as a decoy. It's a clever idea, but I don't know if raiders are that easy to fool, and steel isn't exactly cheap right now. Should we try it and find out?

Okay, here's a catch up for the people arriving from the raid. We've got a small colony on a cold map, a gate that leads somewhere strange, and a company that pays us to poke at it. That's pretty much our whole situation.

Plan for the evening is research, research, and a little more research. We're close to unlocking the better heaters, and the winter isn't going to wait for us. After that, I want to try a quick look through the gate.
Okay, real question for chat while the colonists sleep. If you could add one room to the colony, anything at all, what would it be? I'm leaning toward a library, but I'm open to persuasion.
Last time we were here, the company sent a guy in a suit to inspect the colony. He walked around, wrote a lot of notes, and left without saying a word. We still don't know if we passed.
Tamsin, swap jobs with Bram for the afternoon. You're better at sowing and he's better at hauling, and we keep doing it the other way around for no reason. Let's fix that before the harvest.

So here's what the odd rooms look like if you're new. Yellow carpet, buzzing lights, and walls that are just slightly too far apart. Walking through them on screen is fine, but I wouldn't want to walk through them in real life.

We've got about three days of food left, so tomorrow is a hunting day. Hollis takes the rifle, Scar takes the bow, and they go east where the deer usually are. Everyone else keeps the colony running while they're gone.
Okay, I need a better name for that storage room. Storage room two is boring, and it's the room where all the good stuff lives. I'll think about it later, which means probably never.

Alright, Juniper asked how long this colony has been running. It's about forty days in game and six streams in real life. Feels a lot longer, mostly because of the raids and that one week without a roof.

For the people just joining, the scary noise you just heard was the gate. It does that every few hours, kind of a low groan from somewhere under the floor. We've decided to treat it like a grandfather clock.
Okay, the company's offering a bigger contract with more silver and a longer trip. It also says to bring extra light and to not count the doors on the way in. Do we take it?

Lantern, you've been here since the very first stream, and I noticed. You were there when the shack burned down and when we found the gate. Every time I look at chat, your name is somewhere in it. Thank you for sticking around through all of it.

Okay, I need a second to say something real. This colony would have fallen apart twenty times without you all yelling advice at me. Half the good ideas in this base came from chat. The bad ideas were mine, but the good ones were yours.
Hey, Mara, you're okay, come here. The raid's over and the door held, and nobody's hurt badly. Juno is already on her way with the kit. Sit down by the fire and breathe for a minute, we've got this.

Wren just followed, and hi, welcome to the weirdest little colony on the internet. We've got six colonists, one cat, and a gate that groans at night. Make yourself comfortable, nobody here bites. Except maybe the muffalo, but only when she's hungry.

Honestly, this is my favorite part of a long stream. Everyone in the colony is asleep, the lights are low, and chat is just talking to each other. It feels like a living room at midnight. I really love that we have this.
Pip, buddy, it's fine that the wall fell down. You built it in the rain with wet stone and half a meal in you. Tomorrow we'll build it again together. Go to bed, you did more today than anyone.

Juniper, thank you for the sub, that's so kind. I know things are tight for a lot of people right now, so it really means something. Odessa is going to cook a fancy meal in your honor tonight. It's going to be soup, but fancy soup.

I just want to say Scar has been carrying this colony. She took the night shift for four days straight so the others could heal. She never complains, she just shows up with the rifle. If I could hug a pawn, she'd get the first one.

Hey, Static Fern, don't apologize for the suggestion. It was a good idea, the game just decided to be mean about it. Honestly, I'd try it again in a heartbeat. Keep the ideas coming, please, because I clearly need all the help I can get.

Biscuit's back, hi, I missed you last stream. We kept a seat open for you at the colony table, which is a real table now, with chairs. Pip made them, and only one of them wobbles. You get the good one.
Everybody in chat, say hi to Moss, it's their first stream with us. Moss, you picked a great night, we're about to open a new door in the odd wing. Grab a snack and settle in. You're one of us now.

You know, when I started this colony I didn't think anyone would watch. Now there's a whole crowd of you who know the cat's name and the muffalo's birthday. That's wild to me. Thank you for making this feel like a home.

Odessa, sweetheart, the meal being a little burnt isn't a disaster. Everyone ate it, and Rook asked for seconds. Nobody is upset with you. Go take a break and sit with the cat for a while, you've been at that stove since sunrise.

Nova just gifted five subs and I genuinely don't know what to say. That's so generous, and five people get to hang out here with us now. Welcome, all of you. The colony salutes you, and Socks the cat is purring about it.
I love how this crew takes care of each other. Hollis brought Ivy her dinner in bed because she was too tired to walk. Bram fixed her lamp while she slept. Nobody told them to do any of that.

Chat, it's okay, we didn't lose the colony. It looks scary with everyone downed, but the raiders left and Juno's patching people up. We're going to be fine. Give me a minute to get everyone into bed and I'll show you.

Cobalt, I saw your message about having a rough week. I'm really glad you came here to unwind. Stay as long as you want, there's no pressure to talk. We'll just build some walls together and let the evening be slow and quiet.

Pixel has been answering questions in chat all night while I was busy panicking about the raid. That's such a kind thing to do. You didn't have to, and you did anyway. Thank you, really, I owe you a whole room in the colony.

Tamsin, I know the dark rooms scare you, and that's okay. You don't have to go on this expedition. Stay here and keep the farm alive, that's just as important. We'll be back before supper, and I'll tell you everything we found.

There's something sweet about watching Rook and Socks the cat. Every night she sleeps on his chest, and every morning he wakes up and doesn't move until she leaves. He'll be late for work and he doesn't care. I respect that so much.

Lantern just said this stream is the best part of their day, and I'm not crying, it's just dusty in here. You're the best part of mine too. Seriously, thank you for being here. Okay, back to the farm before I get emotional.

Hey, it's not your fault the raid hit, Ivy. You saw them coming and you rang the bell, that's literally the job. We got everyone inside because of you. Take the rest of the night off and go sit by the heater.

Juno has saved every single person in this colony at least once. She's stitched up Bram three times, Pip twice, and me once, when I tripped on a muffalo. She deserves a medal, or a nicer bed. I'll build the bed.

Everybody take a second and drink some water, real life water. We've been streaming for four hours and I just realized I haven't had any. Stretch your back too, because I can hear mine creaking from here. Okay, now we can go back to the colony.

Hi, Wren, welcome back, and congrats on the new job you mentioned last time. That's huge, I hope the first week was gentle on you. The colony is celebrating with you, sort of. Pip just built a statue, so let's say it's for you.

Bram, look at me, you're home. The odd rooms are behind the door and the door is locked. You're in your own bed with a lamp on. Nothing in there can follow you here, and I'll keep the lights on all night.

Okay, I have to give a shout out to the people who keep the chat kind. Every time someone new shows up, you all greet them like a family reunion. That's rare on the internet. I don't take it for granted.

Hollis just carried the old muffalo into the barn because she couldn't walk through the snow. He didn't have to, there was a path. He just didn't want her cold feet on the ice. That man is too good for this world.

Biscuit, don't worry about missing last stream. Nothing that big happened, I promise, just a lot of farming and one weird door. You'll catch up in five minutes. We saved you a spot right next to the fireplace, the warm one.
Some of you have been here since the colony was just a tent and a campfire. Now we've got walls, a hospital, a gate room, and a cat. You watched every brick go down. That makes this your colony too.

Juno, you did everything you could for him, and he's going to pull through. The fever's dropping and he's sleeping now. Go eat, go rest, and I'll wake you if anything changes. You've been amazing tonight, honestly the best doctor we could ask for.

Static Fern, thank you for the raid, and hello to everyone coming in with you. We're in the middle of a cozy night, so your timing is perfect. Find a seat by the fireplace. Odessa's making stew, and there's plenty for everybody.

You know what I love about this crew? They all have their little habits. Mara hums when she cooks, Pip talks to the plants, and Rook waves at the gate every morning. It makes them feel like real people.

Chat, I see some of you worried about Scar after that fight. She's fine, she's resting in the hospital with her leg wrapped up. Juno says three days of bed rest. She'll be back on the wall before you know it.

I want to thank everyone who sent nice messages after last stream. I was having a rough night and you could tell. You didn't make it weird, you just stayed. That meant more than you know, and I still think about it.

Nova just told me they named their real cat Socks after ours. That is the sweetest thing I've heard all week. Our Socks would be honored, if she cared about anything besides naps. Give your Socks a scratch from us.

Juniper, go get some sleep, it's late where you're. The colony will still be here tomorrow, and I'll catch you up. You've been yawning in chat for an hour. Goodnight, friend, thanks for staying with us so long tonight.

Look at the crew all sitting around the fire after the harvest. Everyone's fed, everyone's warm, and nobody's arguing for once. Ivy's showing Tamsin a card trick that she keeps messing up on purpose. This is why we build walls in the first place.

Pixel, it's totally okay that you can't sub right now. Being here and chatting is the whole thing for me. Honestly, lurkers count too, every single one of you sitting quietly in the back. Everyone who watches is part of this.

Moss just told me they started playing the game because of these streams. That makes me so happy, I can't even explain it. If you ever need help with your colony, ask in here. We'll all help you lose it slower.

Okay, Socks is sitting on the research bench again. She's not researching anything, she's just blocking the queue on purpose. Honestly, she's probably smarter than the rest of us combined, so I'll allow it.

I love that the company's idea of a reward for surviving a breach is a mug. Not silver, not medicine, a mug that says employee of the month. Odessa uses it for tea now, and she drinks it with so much pride. Honestly, fair enough.

Pixel says I play this colony like a raccoon running a hotel, and that's honestly accurate. Things are mostly fine, the guests are mostly fed, and occasionally something is on the roof that shouldn't be. I'm taking it as a compliment.
Juniper wants to know if Scar has ever missed a shot. Technically, no, but she did once shoot a lamp because it looked at her funny. Does that count as a miss if she meant to do it?

Last stream Mara got into a staring contest with the vending machine in the odd wing. She lost. I don't know how you lose a staring contest to a machine, but somehow the machine blinked first and she still lost.

Funny thing about Juno, she's the best doctor we've and she's afraid of the cat. Every time Socks walks into the hospital, Juno climbs onto a bed. She'll stitch up a raider without blinking. But a small orange cat is where she draws the line.

Here's a colonist story for you. Tamsin decided to decorate her room, and by decorate I mean she put eleven plant pots in a room the size of a closet. She can't reach her bed anymore. She sleeps on the floor surrounded by tiny cactuses, and she says she's never been happier.
Okay, I'm not saying I built the kitchen backwards on purpose, but I'm also not saying I didn't. It's a creative layout. People enter through the freezer now and it builds character.

Rook is having a full conversation with the gate right now. He's waving, he's nodding, and he looks very pleased with whatever the gate is saying back. I'm choosing not to ask questions about this one.

So the funniest thing happened on the expedition last night. Scar and Mara walked through the same door twice and came out in the same room twice. On the third try, they just sat down and had lunch in the hallway. Honestly, that's what I would do too.
Hmm, Bram is wearing two hats again. I don't remember giving him two hats. I'm deciding that's a problem for future me, because current me is busy putting out a small fire in the kitchen.

Odessa insists on cooking with the window open, even in winter. Her reason is that the soup needs fresh air. It doesn't, the soup is soup, but nobody's brave enough to argue with the woman holding the ladle.
You know your colony is a little off when the company inspector asks why the cat has a desk. Socks does have a desk. It's in the office, it has a nameplate, and it gets more mail than I do.
Okay, Mara sneezed and dropped her rifle and somehow it still hit a raider. I'm counting that as skill, and I'm writing it in the colony records. Nobody correct me in chat.

Funny anecdote, real quick. Tamsin tried to plant potatoes inside the odd wing because the light is always on in there. They grew, but they grew sideways, out of the wall. We ate them anyway and nobody's turned into anything yet.

Lantern is asking if I've ever just let the cat run the colony for a day. Honestly, we kind of did, last stream, because I was distracted by chat. Did anyone notice that we lost nothing, and the cat got four naps in?
Ivy is the only colonist who talks to the raiders before shooting them. She yells something like, please don't, and then shoots them anyway. Very polite, very fast, honestly my favorite combat style.

Okay, so Cobalt bet in chat that Bram would trip on the stairs today. Bram has never tripped on anything in his life. He tripped on the stairs four minutes later, and now Cobalt is unbearable. Congratulations, you predicted chaos.

Okay, the company just sent a survey asking how we'd rate the odd rooms out of ten. One room ate a chair, one room was a hallway that went nowhere, and one had a very nice lamp. What score do I give that?

We made it through the winter, everybody. Not one colonist lost, not one frostbitten toe, and the freezer is still half full of meat. I was so sure that cold snap was going to break us in the second week. Instead we're all here, warm and fed and a little smug about it.

Juno just finished the surgery and Bram is going to keep his leg. I've been holding my breath for about five minutes straight, and I can finally let it out. He's asleep in the hospital bed now with Socks curled up by his feet. Honestly, best possible outcome tonight.

Finally, the caravan made it home with everything we needed. Medicine, steel, two bags of seeds, and a very confused goat nobody remembers buying. After the week we had, seeing them walk through the front gate felt like a holiday. Welcome home, team, you earned every bit of supper tonight.

Look, the raid's done and we didn't lose anybody. Everybody can stop holding their breath now, me included. The walls held, the turrets held, and Gary the turret is officially a hero. We're good, chat, we're really, really good.

Biscuit, the research finally finished, the heaters are unlocked. I've been waiting on this for three streams and I genuinely thought it would never happen. Every room in the colony is going to be cozy by tonight. Nobody has to sleep in their coat ever again, and I'm so relieved.

Mara came back from the odd wing with a full sample case and no injuries for once. The company is going to pay us double for this one. That means a new hospital bed, better armor, and maybe even a pool table if I'm lucky. Today is a good day, everybody.

Did you see that? Ivy hit the raider from across the whole field on her very first shot of the night. I didn't even know she could shoot that far, and I don't think she did either. Can we all agree she gets the comfy chair at dinner tonight?

Our first real harvest just came in, and look at that pile. Rice, corn, potatoes, and a single giant pumpkin that Tamsin has been guarding like it's treasure. We can actually eat well for a whole season now. I'm so proud of this little farm and everyone who worked it.

Pudding the muffalo had a baby, chat. I didn't even know she was expecting, she's so old, and now there's a tiny fuzzy calf following her around the barn. Hollis is already building it a little bed. This is the best news we've had all week, and I'm smiling way too hard at my screen.

Big news, the company just sent a letter saying our colony is their top performing site this quarter. I have no idea what a quarter means to them, but we're number one at it. There's a bonus attached, and it's actually a real bonus this time. We celebrate with stew tonight.

Pip's fever finally broke, everyone, so you can stop spamming the worried face now. He's sitting up, he's eating, and he's already asking about his rocks. Juno says another day in bed and he's back on hauling. Our little guy pulled through.

Scar and Rook just got back from the expedition and they found a whole room of old canned food. It's not glamorous, but it's three weeks of meals we don't have to farm. I could kiss that yellow carpet right now. Well, maybe not, it's still a little sticky.

Cobalt, thank you for the tip on the turret placement, it totally worked. The raiders came around the side exactly like you said they would. We took them all down without a single person getting hurt. I owe you one, and chat owes you a round of applause.

Tamsin finally finished her sculpture after six days of chipping at a block of marble. It's a muffalo, of course, and it's honestly beautiful. We put it right in the middle of the dining hall. Everybody's mood just went up and I can see it on the bars.

Guess what, the new bedroom wing is done. And every single colonist has their own room now. No more sleeping six to a barracks, no more Pip snoring into somebody's ear. Who wants to take a little tour with me before everybody moves in?

Hollis just came home from a two day hunt with enough meat to fill the freezer to the top. He walked in, set it down, and went straight to bed without saying a word. That's the most Hollis thing ever. Thank you, quiet king, we're eating well for weeks.

Hey, everybody take a breath, the gate closed on its own and nothing came through. I know that groan was loud, but it was just the gate settling for the night. Everyone's safe inside, and the door's locked. We're totally fine.

I just checked and we have more silver than we've ever had at once. Two whole thousand, sitting in a little room behind the kitchen. For a colony that started with a tent and four potatoes, that's huge. I'm going to look at it for a minute before I spend all of it.

Juniper's prediction came true, the trader showed up today with exactly the medicine we needed. Twenty packs, fair price, no weird hats. I'm so relieved, because the hospital was running on bandages and hope. Now we can actually heal people properly.

After three tries, the solar panels are finally connected the right way. The first time I wired them backwards, the second time Pip unplugged them for a lamp. This time it worked, and the batteries are filling up nice and steady. Small win, but I'll take it.

Look at this, the odd wing gave us something good for once, a room full of working lamps that never need power. We moved them all into the bedrooms and the colony feels so much warmer now. Nobody's afraid of the dark anymore. That's a real gift, even from a strange place.

We hit a thousand followers while I was fighting that raid and I didn't even notice. A thousand people chose to hang out in this weird colony with me. Thank you, every single one of you, I'm beyond grateful. Is that real, or did I just misread the number?

Rook and Ivy are officially a couple now, chat, it popped up in the notifications. They've been sitting together at every meal for two weeks, so nobody's shocked. Still, look at them, they're adorable. Somebody build them a bigger bed.

Nova suggested we try a greenhouse in the odd wing, and it's thriving. The lights never turn off in there, so the crops grow day and night. We're going to have strawberries in winter, real strawberries. That might be the best idea anyone in chat has ever had.

Mara walked out of the hospital today after almost two weeks in bed. She's limping a little, but she went straight to the kitchen and made everyone breakfast. That's who she's. I'm really happy to have her back on her feet.

You can relax, Pixel, the colonist we lost track of is home. Bram walked through the front door about a minute ago like nothing happened, carrying a lamp. He's tired and hungry, but he's okay. I'm so relieved I could cry.

Chat, the company sent us a new contract with no small print, no warnings, and no instructions about doors. It's literally just deliver ten meals to an office. I've never been this happy to do a boring job. We are absolutely taking this one.

Pip managed to tame the squirrel that lives in the barn, and now it follows him everywhere. It rides on his shoulder while he hauls, it sleeps in his pocket at night. They're best friends and it's the sweetest thing. I didn't know I needed this today.

Wow, the rain finally came after nine days of drought. Every plant in the fields is perking up at once and the colonists are standing outside in it on purpose. Tamsin's literally spinning in a circle. I feel like spinning in a circle too, honestly.

We beat the raid with every colonist standing and we only lost one wall. One wall, that's nothing, Pip can rebuild it before lunch. Last time a raid this size hit us we were in the hospital for a week. Look how far we've come, chat.

Static Fern just told me they finally beat their own colony's first winter using the tips from this stream. That makes me so happy. I love that this little corner of the internet helps people keep their pawns alive. Go celebrate, you earned it.

Juno finished training an apprentice, and it's Ivy. Now we have two people who can patch up a gunshot wound, which honestly takes a lot of pressure off. Juno can finally sleep through a whole night. I'm thrilled for both of them.

Wren, your sub just came in at the perfect moment, right as the last raider ran off. That's lucky, that's a good omen right there. Thank you so much for the support. The colony and I are both grinning about it.

We finally have enough steel to build the second freezer, and it's done. Two whole freezers, both humming away and full of food. I feel like a responsible adult for the first time in this colony's history. Somebody take a screenshot, this won't last.

Lantern, guess what, the deer that chased Hollis is gone. It wandered off this morning, and he finally walked through the yard without running. He looked so proud of himself. Freedom tastes good, and he's eating his breakfast on the porch.

Everybody passed the company inspection today, every single colonist. The guy in the suit even nodded at the cat. That's the closest thing to approval we've ever gotten from that office. I'll take it, and I'll frame the nod.

It's officially our hundredth day in the colony. When we started, I honestly didn't think we'd last ten. Now there are eight colonists, three buildings, two freezers, and a cat with a desk. Happy hundredth, everybody, we did this together.

Odessa just brought out a birthday cake for Pip. Somebody in the colony keeps track of these things and it's not me. Pip's so surprised he dropped his rock. Happy birthday, little hauler, you deserve a party and the biggest slice.

Good news, the trader came back and this time they had exactly the bionic arm Scar needs. We've been saving silver for weeks for this moment. She's getting her arm tonight, chat. She's going to be absolutely unstoppable once Juno finishes the surgery.

Listen, the colony beat the plague with no deaths. Five people sick at once, two doctors working in shifts, and a whole lot of soup. Everybody's recovering now, slowly but surely. I'm so relieved I'm practically melting into my chair.

I just realized we haven't had a single mental break all week. Everyone's moods are green, the beds are comfy, and the food is good. That's never happened before in this colony. We're actually doing it right, finally, after all these weeks.

Moss's raid strategy worked perfectly, and I'm so happy I could yell. We lured them into the long hallway and the turrets did the rest. Nobody even got a scratch. Moss, you're officially on the colony defense council, sorry, no pay.

Chat, the gate is opening on its own, and it's opening wider than it ever has. There's light coming through, real daylight, not that flickery yellow stuff. I don't know where it goes but I need to know right now. Scar, grab your gear, we're going in.

Whoa, the company just offered us the big contract, the one with the vault. And we said yes. It's three rooms deep, there's a reward at the end that they won't even describe, and we have two days to prepare. I'm so hyped, I can barely sit still in this chair.

Everybody get to the gate room, right now, there's a new door. It just appeared in the wall behind the turret, and it's blue, which we've never seen before. Scar, Mara, bring lights and medicine. We're opening it together, and I want chat watching.

We're two research points away from unlocking the drop pods. Two. Once that finishes, we can send colonists anywhere on the map in seconds. Expeditions are about to get so much faster, and I already have a list of places I want to visit.

Juniper just asked if we're doing the big expedition tonight, and you know what? Yes, we're, all six of us, no backups, full send. The colony's stocked, the weather's calm, and I'm feeling lucky. Are you ready to see what's in the deep rooms?

Yes, the deep rooms are open, chat. We've been stuck at the third door for a whole week and it finally unlocked. There's a staircase going down, and I can hear the generators humming below. Mara, you're in front, go go go.

I just got word that a meteor is landing near the colony, and it's made of gold. Gold, as in shiny money gold. Pip's already running toward it with a pickaxe. I've never seen him move that fast, not even for dinner.

We unlocked the advanced turrets and I'm about to build like four of them. The raiders don't stand a chance anymore, not even the big ones. Gary is getting friends. I'm calling the new one Gary Two, because I'm not creative and I don't care.

There's a trader at the gate who says they sell maps of the odd wing. Real maps, all the rooms, every hallway. I want to buy every single one of them right now. Which one should we grab first, chat, the blue rooms or the deep rooms?

This is the moment we've been building toward since day one. The ship parts are done, the reactor is ready, and we just need to survive fifteen days. Fifteen days, and then we fly out of here. I'm so excited I'm shaking a little.

Somebody go wake up Hollis, there's a herd of muffalo walking across the map. Like thirty of them, all fuzzy, all slow, all ours if we're quick. Grab the ropes, everybody, we're taming as many as we can. This is the best thing that's happened all day.

Hey, the company says if we finish this contract, we get access to the headquarters. The actual headquarters, the building nobody's ever been inside. I've wanted to see it since the very first stream. We have to finish this, we have to, there's no other option.

We're about to open the vault, and I've been saving this for the end of the stream. I don't know what's inside, the company won't tell us, and neither will the map. Everybody get in chat and make your guesses. Three, two, one, opening.

Wren, did you see that? The new colonist just joined and she's a master builder with level twenty construction. We can finally build the big hall I've been dreaming about. Should I start drawing it up right now while we're all excited?

Alright, chat, the ship is launching, chat, it's actually launching. After all of this, the raids and the rooms and the paperwork, we're actually leaving the planet. I can't believe we made it. Everybody say goodbye to the colony, we're going home.

There's a new room in the odd wing and it's full of furniture. Not broken stuff, like real, nice, matching furniture. Beds, chairs, a whole dining set. I'm redecorating the entire colony tonight, so nobody try to stop me.

Our first ever animal birth from a tamed thrumbo just happened, and I'm actually screaming inside. Thrumbos are so rare and so valuable, and now we have a baby one. It's tiny and it's white and it's ours. Hollis is going to cry, I just know it.

Everyone vote right now, because this is a big one. Option one, we take the rich contract and send our three best fighters. Option two, we stay home and finish the walls before winter. Type one or two and let's make a choice in the next minute.

Wait, wait, wait, is that a ship part crashing down by the river? It is, and it's still smoking, which means there's loot inside and probably angry robots too. Can somebody please tell me we have enough turrets for this?

Grab the rifles and line up behind the sandbags, everybody, here they come. This is the biggest raid we've ever seen, and we planned for exactly this. Hold the line, wait for my call, and then let them have it. We've got this.

Just unlocked the company elevator and I need you all to see where it goes. The buttons go all the way down to floor negative forty. Nobody's ever pressed the bottom one, at least nobody who came back to tell about it. We're pressing it right now.

Cobalt just dropped a raid with sixty people, welcome, welcome, all of you. You showed up at the perfect moment, because we're about to open the blue door for the very first time. Where do you think it leads, the beach or the basement?

Mara just leveled her shooting to fifteen and I'm screaming. She started this colony unable to hit a barn from inside the barn. Now she's taking raiders down from across the river like it's nothing. Look at my girl go.

Honestly, I've waited forty streams for this, and here it's, the eclipse event. The odd rooms are going to shift around and new doors are going to show up everywhere. It's like the map is reshuffling itself just for us. I'm ready, I've been ready since breakfast.

Quick, everybody pick a colonist to cheer for in the race to the gate. Pip is fast but distracted, Rook is slow but steady, and Ivy is just chaotic. Type your pick in chat right now. Winner gets bragging rights and nothing else.

Just a heads up, the caravan from the north brought a mechanoid core, and I can build a helper robot. A little robot that hauls and cleans and never complains. I'm naming it Toaster and I'm building it immediately. Pip is going to be so jealous.

Nova, you said you've never seen a thrumbo in person, right? Well, look at the top of the map, because there's one walking right past the colony. It's huge, it's white, and it's gorgeous. Want me to try taming it live?

Here we go, chat, the final wave of the siege. If we survive this one, the company says the contract is complete and the reward unlocks. I'm sweating and I'm not even the one with a gun. Turrets on, doors closed, let's finish this.

Rook just found a hidden staircase behind the bookshelf in the library. A literal secret passage, like in a movie. I had no idea that room had anything behind it, and I built it myself. We're exploring it right after the meal break, and I can barely wait.

Get the cameras ready, chat, Bram's about to try the jump across the broken bridge in the odd wing. If he makes it, we unlock the far side of the map. If he doesn't, Juno has the medkit standing by. Go, Bram, go.

Just watched three different factions declare peace with us in the same morning. That means trade routes, allies for raids, and nobody burning our crops for a while. This is huge, this changes everything for the next season. I'm already planning a trade trip.

We found the company's lost courier inside the deep rooms, and she's alive. She's been stuck down there for weeks surviving on vending machine snacks. The reward for bringing her home is enormous. Everybody get the stretcher, we're carrying her out.

Static Fern just pointed out the new event in the quest log, a festival from the neighbor faction. There's dancing, there's food, and there's a raffle for a gold sculpture. Who are we sending to represent the colony?

Here's the plan for tomorrow, and I'm so pumped about it. We take the drop pods to the ancient ruins across the map, crack open the sealed room, and fly back before nightfall. Scar, Mara, and Rook are going, with Juno on the radio. It's going to be legendary.

Pixel just hit a whole year of being subscribed, chat, a whole year. That means you've been here since the very first colony, the one that burned down in a week. You've seen it all, the good and the very bad. Let's go, Pixel, happy anniversary.

There's an anomaly in the sky over the colony, and it's not a solar flare this time. It's purple, it's glowing, and the colonists keep stopping to look at it. I have no idea what it does yet. I'm thrilled and terrified in equal parts right now.

Lantern, you asked if we'd ever try the hardest contract on the board, and the answer is today. It's rated deadly, it pays a fortune, and it has a room called the hungry hallway. Should we stream the whole thing from start to finish?

Hold on, Ivy hasn't come back from the odd wing yet. She was only supposed to grab one sample and walk out, and that was two hours ago in game. The radio's quiet, and that's never a good sign. I'm sending Scar in after her right now.

Has anybody else noticed Bram hasn't eaten in two days? He keeps walking past the dining room and just staring at the gate. I think something in there got to him. Should I lock him in his room until Juno can take a look?

Everybody stay away from the north wall tonight. Something keeps scratching at it from the outside, and the turrets aren't picking anything up. Keep the lights on, sleep in pairs, and nobody goes out for a walk. I mean it, nobody.

Our food is lower than I thought, and I'm a little worried. We've got maybe four days of meals left, the crops aren't ready, and the trader isn't due for a week. I need to send hunters out tomorrow morning. Otherwise we're going to be eating berries again.

Juno, I know you're exhausted, but you need to sleep. You've been in the hospital for thirty hours straight and you're starting to make mistakes. Ivy can watch the patients for a while. Go lie down, I'll wake you up if anything happens.
Pip came back from the expedition with a strange mark on his arm, and he won't tell anyone where he got it. Juno says it's not a burn and it's not a cut. What do you all think it could be?

Something about this raid feels off. They're not attacking, they're just standing at the edge of the map, waiting. It's been an hour and they haven't moved an inch. I don't like it one bit, and I'm keeping everyone inside.

Mara, step back from that door right now. It's warm on our side and it shouldn't be, and I can hear something humming on the other side. We'll come back with more people and more light. Not today, not alone.

Moss, you mentioned your colony lost everyone to the same kind of storm last week, right? It's heading our way right now, and I've never seen one this dark. Do you remember what killed them, was it the cold or the lightning?

Tamsin's mood is dropping fast and I'm not sure why. She was fine this morning, then she walked past the empty bedroom and just stopped smiling. I think she's thinking about Hollis. I'm going to give her the day off and let her rest by the fire.

Hey, Pixel, it's okay that you were worried when the stream froze for a bit. My internet just took a nap for a second, and nothing happened in the colony while it was out. Everyone's fine, I promise. I'm right here, and so is the cat, still asleep on the desk.

Rook's been coughing all week and it's getting worse. Juno thinks it could be the start of the plague that hit the neighbors. If it's, we need to quarantine him before it spreads. I really hope she's wrong about this one.

Chat, I need your eyes on the minimap for a minute. The gate's been groaning every few seconds instead of every few hours. Tell me the moment anything walks out of it. Something's changed and I don't know what yet.

Hmm, the company hasn't sent a single message in three days. They always send something, a memo, a form, a complaint about our handwriting. Silence from them feels worse than the paperwork. I keep checking the phone and it's just quiet.

Is it just me, or is the odd wing getting closer to the bedrooms every night? I measured it last stream and it was twelve tiles away from Tamsin's door. Now it's ten. Am I losing track of things, or did the hallway actually move on its own?

Odessa, sweetie, it's okay to be scared of the dark rooms. Nobody's going to make you go in there, not today and not ever. You can stay in the kitchen where it's warm and bright and smells like bread. We'll handle the scary stuff, I promise.

Bram woke up in the middle of the night and walked straight to the gate in his sleep. Rook caught him just before he touched it. Nobody knows why he did it, including Bram. I'm putting a lock on his door tonight, just to be safe.

We're heading into the coldest week of the year with only half the firewood we need. If the heaters fail, we're in real trouble. I've got everybody chopping trees, but the forest is thin this close to the colony. Let's hope the weather is kind for once.

Wren just asked something that's been bothering me too. Why did the raiders walk right past the turrets without shooting, and go straight to the gate room instead? What do they know about it that we don't?

Juniper, you've been here for six hours, please go eat something. I can see you in chat at three in the morning your time. The colony will be fine without you watching, I promise. Go take care of yourself first.

Ivy's arm is getting infected, and the medicine we've isn't strong enough. Juno's doing her best, but she needs the glitterworld kind. The nearest trader is two days away. I'm sending a runner right now and hoping we're fast enough.

Biscuit, I saw your message about the bad day you're having, and I'm sorry. You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to. Just hang out here with us, watch the cat nap. We're happy you're here.

Something's wrong with the water from the well near the odd wing. Everyone who drank it this morning is acting a bit sleepy and slow. I'm blocking the well off until Juno can test it. Nobody drinks from it again until we know.

Cobalt, do you think we should send the expedition out with the storm coming? I've got a bad feeling about it, but the contract only lasts two more days. I don't want to lose the reward, but I'd rather not lose a colonist either. Is it worth the risk?

Honestly, the muffalo hasn't moved from her corner of the barn all day. She's old, chat, very old, and I think she might be getting sick. Hollis is sitting with her right now. I'm not ready for what this might mean.

Everyone check your armor before you step through that gate. Last time Mara went in with a broken helmet and came back with a concussion. Juno, do a quick look at everyone's gear. We're not losing anyone to a silly mistake today.
Scar, you don't have to be the one who goes first every single time. I know you feel responsible for everybody, but you need rest too. Rook can take point on this one. Stay home and heal up, okay?
Pip has been sitting alone in the odd wing for an hour, just staring at a wall. He's not hurt, he's not scared, he's just quiet. It's not like him at all. I'm going to go check on him myself.
Static Fern asked if we're ready for the siege, and honestly, I'm not sure we're. We've got enough ammo for a short fight and not much else. How long do you think we can hold out?

Juno's been working nonstop since the raid and she's starting to break down. Her mood bar is red and she's talking to herself in the hospital. I'm making her stop, even though we still have patients. She can't take care of anyone if she falls apart.

Lantern, I know the colony looks rough right now, but we've been through worse than this. Half the walls are down, two people are hurt, and we're low on food. We're still standing, though, all of us. We'll rebuild tomorrow, we always do.

Ugh, the gate just spat out a colonist I've never seen before. She's wearing a company uniform, she's injured, and she won't say a single word. I'm keeping her in the hospital under watch. Something about this feels very, very wrong.

Everybody take a look at the temperature, because it's dropping fast. If it hits freezing, the crops die and we lose half our food for the season. Haul everything you can inside and close the greenhouse doors. Move fast, please.

Is anyone else worried about how quiet the colony's been tonight? No raids, no events, no company memos, not even a groan from the gate. That never happens here, not even once in forty days. Do you think something big is coming for us?

Mara, I know losing the fight hurt, but you're going to be okay. Juno set your arm and it's going to heal clean. You'll be shooting again in a week, I promise. For now, just rest and let's take care of things.

Pudding passed away in her sleep last night. She was the oldest muffalo on the map and she lived a really good life, warm barn, lots of hay, Hollis brushing her every morning. I knew this day was coming, but it still hurts. Rest easy, sweet girl.

We lost Hollis in the raid tonight. He held the door so the others could get inside, and he didn't make it back. He never complained, not once, the whole time we knew him. I don't really know what to say right now, chat.

Tamsin hasn't left Hollis's grave all morning. She brought flowers from the greenhouse, the yellow ones he liked, and she just sat there in the grass. Nobody's telling her to come in, we're just letting her be. Some things you can't fix with a work schedule.
It's quiet in the dining hall without Pip. His chair is still there, and nobody's sitting in it. Odessa still made his favorite stew tonight out of habit. I think we all just kind of ate it for him.

I read the company letter about Ivy, and it was one line long. Your employee has been reassigned. That's it, after everything she did for this colony. I miss her already, and I don't even know where she went.

This is the last stream of this colony, and I'm a little emotional about it. We've been here a hundred and twenty days, through raids and plagues and all those weird rooms. I'm going to miss these people. Thank you for being here for all of it.

Socks the cat didn't come home last night. She's never done that, not once, she always sleeps on Rook's chest. We looked everywhere, the barn, the kitchen, even the odd wing. I really hope she just found a warm spot somewhere.

Juno blames herself for losing Bram on the operating table. She did everything right, she really did, and it just wasn't enough. I keep telling her that, but I don't think she hears it yet. It's going to take time for all of us.
Last stream, if you missed it, we lost Mara in the deep rooms. She went in to grab one last sample and the door closed behind her. We waited for two days by that door. It never opened again.

I built a little memorial garden by the river today. One flower for each colonist we've lost, and there are more of them than I'd like. It's a nice spot, though, quiet and green. I think they'd like it there.

Rook still waves at the gate every morning, even though Ivy went through it and never came back. He just stands there for a minute, waves, and then goes to work. Nobody has the heart to stop him. Honestly, I don't want anybody to.

Here's a reflective one before we wrap up for the night. This colony started with four people, and only one of them is still here, which is Scar. Everyone else either left, got lost, or didn't make it. She carries all of them with her, I think.

Odessa's birthday is today, and Pip used to bake her a cake every year. This year nobody remembered until the evening. I asked her about it, and she just said it's okay. It isn't, though, and I'm sorry, Odessa.

Real talk, the empty bed in the barracks is the hardest part. Every night I look at the colony from above and it's just sitting there, made up and quiet. I can't bring myself to deconstruct it yet. Maybe next stream, maybe not.

Wren just told me their real dog passed away this week, and I'm so sorry. You've watched us lose colonists and cried with us in chat. It's okay to bring the real sad stuff here too. We'll sit with you as long as you need.

We had to leave the old colony behind when the odd wing swallowed it. Everything we built, the farm, the kitchen, the sculpture of the muffalo, it's all gone now. We got the people out, and that's what matters. Still, I'm going to miss that place.

At the end of a long colony, I always look back at the first day. A tent, a campfire, three nervous colonists, and no idea what was coming. It's strange how much a little world can mean to you. I think I'll keep the save, just to visit.

Bram's last words in the game log were that he wanted to see the sea. We never found a coast, not once, the whole map is forest. I keep thinking about that. I'm naming the river after him, so maybe it can carry him there.

Pip's squirrel keeps waiting by his bedroom door, even now. Every night it curls up there on the little rug and won't move until morning. Animals know, I think, more than we give them credit for. It's the saddest little thing I've ever seen in this game.

I just realized this is the last time I'll hear the gate groan. The colony ends tonight, and with it all those strange rooms and the company's paperwork. It's silly to miss a noise, but I do. Thank you for spending all those nights here with me.

Scar's sitting alone on the roof again, staring at the stars. She does that every night since Mara disappeared. I gave her a warm coat and a lamp, that's about all I can do. Sometimes being there's the only thing that helps.

Lantern asked if I'm okay after losing Juno, and honestly, not really. She was the heart of this colony, the one who kept everybody going. Losing her feels like losing the walls. We'll keep going, but it's not the same.

We buried the company courier by the river today. We never even learned her name, she never spoke, not once. Still, she was one of us for a little while. I put a lamp on her grave so she won't be in the dark.

I'm going to miss this crew so much. The mornings with Odessa's soup, the nights with Rook guarding the gate, Pip's rocks on my bedside table. These were good people, even if they were only pixels. Thank you for loving them with me.

Here's a story from last stream that I didn't have the heart to tell then. The night before the raid, Hollis sat with Tamsin by the fire and told her everything would be okay. He knew it might not be. That's who he was, right to the end.

Ivy's room is exactly how she left it. Her bed is made, her little plant is still on the windowsill, and her coat is on the hook. Tamsin waters the plant every morning. I don't think we'll ever move anything in there.

We lost the colony to the cold tonight, chat. The heaters failed, the snow kept coming, and one by one everybody just slowed down. I'm not angry, just quiet. It was a good run, and I loved every minute of it.

Odessa left the colony today to join the traders heading south. She said she'd be back someday, but I don't really think she will. The kitchen feels so empty without her humming over the stove. Safe travels, Odessa, wherever you end up.

Looking back over this whole colony, the thing I'll remember most isn't the raids or the strange rooms. It's the quiet evenings, everybody gathered around the fire, chat talking softly. Those were the moments that mattered. I'm really going to miss them, more than I expected.

Juniper, thank you for the kind words about Mara. She really was something special, wasn't she? I keep looking for her in the kitchen at breakfast. I guess part of me still expects her to walk through the door.
Why does the cooler keep breaking again and again I turn my back? I fixed it this morning, I fixed it at lunch, and now it's broken again. Pip, stop leaning on it, please, I'm begging you.

Third raid this week, and it's two in the morning again. Every time the colony finally gets to sleep, a pack of raiders shows up with torches. I just want one quiet night. Is that really too much to ask from this planet?
Why is Bram hauling rocks into the hospital? I set the zone, I set it twice, I triple checked it on stream. What part of the hospital looks like a rock storage room to him?
Nope, the wall collapsed again. That's three times now, and I used real stone this time, not wood, and I even checked the roof supports. Note to self, never build walls in the rain with Pip.

Right, the company just sent another form asking me to fill out the same form I filled out yesterday. And the day before that, too, word for word. I'm starting to think they don't read them at all. Honestly, I'm starting to think there's no one in that office.
How did the fire spread to the freezer? The freezer is made of stone, the freezer is cold, the freezer should not be on fire. What did I do to deserve this?

We lost the whole potato crop to blight, again, right before harvest. I put the greenhouse in specifically so this wouldn't happen. It happened anyway, inside the greenhouse, behind a closed door. I give up on potatoes, I really do, we're a rice colony now.
Ugh, I misclicked and sent Rook through the gate instead of Scar. Rook doesn't even have a weapon, he has a shovel and a sandwich. Come back, Rook, come back right now before something notices you.

each time, no exceptions I open the trade menu, the trader decides to leave. Every time, right as I finally find the item I want. They just turn around, pack up the mules, and walk off the map. I'm starting to take this very personally.

Can somebody please explain why the turret shot at the cat? Socks was nowhere near the raiders, she was sitting on the porch minding her own business. Is Gary just angry at everything now, or does he have a grudge?

I've told Pip a hundred times not to touch the vending machine in the odd wing. He touched the vending machine. Now his sleeve is gone, his hat is gone, and he's somehow covered in soda from head to toe. I'm so tired, chat.

Why does every colonist have a mental break at the exact same moment? One person cries, then another person cries, and then Bram starts throwing food across the dining room. Who planned this, honestly, and can I speak to them?

Ten days of mining in game, and the vein ran out right before we hit the good stuff. Ten whole days. Pip just stood there holding his pickaxe and staring at the wall. I know exactly how he feels, buddy, I really do.
Hmm, no, that's not right either. I keep rotating the bed and it keeps facing the wall no matter which button I press. Why is this the hardest part of the whole stream, harder than the raid?

Oh, the solar flare hit right in the middle of the surgery, of course it did. Lights out, monitors down, and Juno working by candlelight. She managed it anyway, but my heart can't take this. Why does the game time these so perfectly?

This is the fourth time a raid has walked straight past my perfect kill zone. I built the hallway, I built the turrets, I built the decoy. They just walked around the side like it wasn't even there. I need a better plan, clearly.

Rook, put down the shovel and go to bed. You've been digging that same hole since sunrise and it isn't going anywhere. It's two in the morning, my friend, and your sleep bar is empty. Go to sleep, please, I'm asking nicely.

We had enough silver for the bionic arm, and I accidentally spent it on a painting. A painting of a rock, which Pip loves more than anything. Scar is going to be so annoyed when she finds out. I'm so annoyed at myself right now.

Did the raiders seriously just steal our only medicine? Out of everything in the stockpile, the silver, the steel, the fancy rugs, they went straight for the medicine. Couldn't they have taken the rock painting instead?

Nope, nope, nope, the mood bar is red for everybody again. I just fixed it ten minutes ago with a new rug and a nicer table. Somebody tell me who keeps ruining the dining room, because I'm going to find out.

I've rebuilt the bridge over the river three times now. The first time a flood took it, the second time a raid burned it, and the third time Bram deconstructed it by accident. I'm leaving it gone. We'll just swim.
What does the company even want from me? I sent the samples, I filled out the forms, and I signed every page they mailed us. Now they want a report on the report, and I'm supposed to have it by noon?

My colonists will walk across the entire map to eat a single berry, but they won't walk five steps to fix a broken heater. I don't understand their priorities. It's freezing in the bedroom and Pip is out picking blueberries. Unbelievable.
Wait, why is the door locked? I didn't lock the door, I would remember locking the door. Oh, I did lock the door, last night, and now Juno can't reach the patient on the other side.

We're out of steel, again, and the trader won't be back for a week. I asked everyone to stop building fancy lamps, and somebody built a fancy lamp anyway. It's a very nice lamp, I'll admit. I'm still annoyed about it.

Everybody stop moving for one second. Something in the colony keeps setting itself on fire and I need to figure out what it's. Freeze where you're, all of you, even you, Pip. Thank you, now I can actually find it.

Apparently the colony is overcrowded, according to the alert. We have six people and nine bedrooms. How is that crowded, chat, when half the beds are empty every night? I'm checking the numbers again, because somebody is clearly sleeping in the freezer.

One raider has escaped three raids in a row. He runs in, takes one shot, and runs away before the turrets even notice him. I'm naming him Mister Torch, and he's officially my nemesis now. Next time, Mister Torch, next time.

Third time trying to tame the thrumbo and it just won't happen. I've got the food, I've got the best handler, and the thrumbo keeps walking away. I'm about to give up and just admire it from a distance. It's very pretty, at least.

Rook, listen to me, losing the crop wasn't your fault at all. The blight hit every farm on the map this season, even the neighbors lost theirs. We have rice in the freezer and a trader coming, so nobody's going hungry this winter.

Nobody in chat needs to feel bad about backseating, I asked for it. Half my best ideas come from you yelling at me when I forget the cooler. Keep yelling, honestly, the colony depends on it more than I like to admit.

Tamsin, honey, it's alright to miss him. Hollis was your best friend in this place, and missing him means he mattered. Take all the time you need by the river, and we'll keep a plate warm for you at supper.

Moss, you didn't break anything by suggesting the new door. The game just threw a raid at us, that's what it does. Your idea was good and the colony is still standing, so please don't feel guilty about it.

Hey, Ivy, you're safe now, the door's closed behind you. Whatever was in that hallway can't reach the bedrooms. Sit on the bed, drink some water, and let Juno take a look at that scratch when you're ready.

Juniper, it's fine that you fell asleep during the stream last night. Honestly, that's a compliment, it means the colony was cozy enough to nap to. I'll catch you up on the two things that happened while you were out.
Bram, buddy, the statue doesn't have to be perfect. Everybody loved it the moment you put it in the hall, even with the lopsided ear. It's yours, and that's what makes it special to all of us.

Biscuit, don't stress about the subscription ending. You're here, you're in chat, you're part of the family regardless. The colony doesn't care about badges and neither do I, so stay as long as you like.
Pip, I know the squirrel ran away, but I bet it comes back by morning. It always does, it just likes to explore the barn rafters at night. Leave a little nut by the door and get some sleep, okay?

Static Fern, you can absolutely ask questions even if they feel basic. Everyone here started somewhere, including me, and I burned down my first kitchen in a day. Ask anything, there's no wrong question in this chat.
Odessa, you don't need to cook for everyone tonight. Take the evening off and let Bram make his terrible sandwiches for once. We'll survive one night of bad food, and you deserve a break by the fire.
Wren, it's totally okay to lurk. You don't have to talk to be part of this, just hanging out counts. I see your name in the viewer list every stream and it makes me smile every time.

Mara, it's okay that you froze up in the fight. Everybody freezes sometimes, especially the first time something comes out of the gate. You came back, and you're safe, and that's all that matters tonight.
Cobalt, I promise we're not giving up on this colony. It looks rough, sure, but we've climbed out of worse holes than this. Give it two streams and you won't even recognize the place.

Scar, you protected everyone today, and nobody blames you for the wall. You held the line by yourself for almost an hour. Go get some rest, you have more than earned it, and I'll take the night watch.
Nova, the colony's going to be fine while I'm away this weekend. Nothing moves when the stream's off, the colonists just wait for us. We'll pick up right where we left off on Monday, I promise.
Lantern, you don't have to apologize for missing a few streams. Life happens, and the colony isn't going anywhere. It's just nice to see you back, and Socks remembers you, I'm pretty sure.
Juno, you're not alone in that hospital anymore. Ivy's learning fast, and she'll be able to handle the small stuff by next week. You can share the load now, so please let her help you.

Pixel, it's okay if the game feels overwhelming when you start. It took me three failed colonies before I figured out the freezer. Go slow, build a small room first, and come ask us whenever you get stuck.
Hollis, you can stop pacing by the window, the hunting party is fine. They radioed in an hour ago, everybody's safe and they're bringing back a deer. Sit down and have some tea while you wait.
Hey chat, I know a lot of you were nervous about the expedition. Everybody made it home, a little scratched up but whole. Let's take a breath together before we decide what to do next.

Tamsin, it's alright that the garden didn't make it this year. The ground was frozen, nobody could have saved it. We'll plant it again in the spring, together, and it's going to be the prettiest one yet.
Juniper, stop worrying about the gift sub, it's genuinely not a big deal. I'd rather you keep your money for something you need. Being here's more than enough, honestly, I mean that.
Rook, you don't have to be brave all the time. It's okay to be scared of the deep rooms, I'm scared of them too. Stay in the colony this time, and we'll go in together when you're ready.
Moss, your colony dying doesn't make you bad at the game. Mine have died in more ways than I can count. You learned something, and next time you'll be ready, I promise.
Pip, you're not in trouble for the rock collection. It's taking up a whole shelf, sure, but it makes you happy. We'll just build another shelf for the actual supplies.
Everyone breathe, the gate made that awful noise but nothing came through. It just does that sometimes, like an old house settling at night. I'm watching it closely, so you can relax for a minute.
Static Fern, it's okay that you're having a rough night. You came here, and that was a good call. Stay as long as you want, and if you need a distraction, we're about to name a goat.
Ivy, you don't have to finish the wall tonight. It's late, you're tired, and the wall will still need building in the morning. Go to bed, and I'll make sure nothing gets through the gap tonight.
Cobalt, don't worry, I saved the colony before the crash. We lost maybe ten minutes of building at most. Everybody's still alive, the cat's still on her desk, and we're picking right back up.
Odessa, the burnt bread isn't the end of the world. Honestly, Pip eats the burnt ones on purpose because he says they taste like campfire. Throw another batch in, we've got plenty of flour.
